pixel_heart.description: A pixel-art heart extruded into a field of small 3D cubes on a single MultiMesh (one draw call). The 'love' reaction in the project's own cube vocabulary — warm red voxels, beveled, readable across a room.
pixel_heart.name: Pixel Heart
pixel_heart.qfep_connection: A reaction is a primitive feeling, so it is a primitive object — the heart was always pixels; we gave the pixels depth.

pixel_thumb.description: A pixel-art thumbs-up extruded into a field of small 3D cubes on a single MultiMesh (one draw call). The 'friend / approved' reaction in the project's own cube vocabulary — cool blue voxels, beveled.
pixel_thumb.name: Pixel Thumb
pixel_thumb.qfep_connection: The thumb says yes in the grammar of the grid — the catalyst's foe-to-friend arc made into a solid object.

floating_sphere_field.description: A sparse field of soft drifting spheres in the void — most of them light, a few of them matter, split across two GPUParticles3D emitters because a particle system has exactly one material. The subtle successor to the Kusama dot-grid biome layer — presence-by-scarcity instead of overwhelming repetition. Ambient atmosphere for the void around the player.
floating_sphere_field.name: Floating Sphere Field
floating_sphere_field.qfep_connection: The void was never empty, only under-rendered. Replacing the lattice with a drift trades the comfort of fixed coordinates for the truth that presence does not require a position — the F term loosening before λE(S).

xyz_slider_plate.description: Dieter Rams plate with three sliders (X, Y, Z) that move a glowing point through space. Live coordinate display and line to origin. Teaches axis independence — moving one slider doesn't affect the others.
xyz_slider_plate.name: XYZ Slider Plate
xyz_slider_plate.qfep_connection: Axis independence as felt experience — the hand learns that three degrees of freedom are orthogonal by moving each one alone.

laser_sword.description: Grabbable glowing blade on a Rams handle — pick it up and the blade ignites with a layered hum. Swing speed modulates pitch and glow intensity. Teaches directed line segment as embodied intention.
laser_sword.name: Laser Sword
laser_sword.qfep_connection: Direction as embodied will — the blade points where you point, making directed line segment a felt experience before a mathematical concept.

dna.default: repose=dark - the last line of _ready was `_blade_mesh.visible = false`, and the dark branch does exactly that and nothing else: blade_length, blade_emission, alpha 0.85, UNSHADED, hidden, hum at -80 dB, which is the state _build_blade already left behind. _ignite now sets length, emission, alpha and shading explicitly, and every one of those assignments is a no-op under dark because nothing has touched them - so a picked-up sword is identical to before under every value. apply_grid_config restyles only when a repose key both validates and differs, only after _ready, and never mid-swing; none of the 22 placements passes one, so all 22 keep a dark blade.
dna.was: no axis at all - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The nine exports are two lengths, two radii, two colours, an emission scalar and three audio numbers: dimensions, decoration and sound. The one decision that decides what this object IS when you look at it - whether there is a line at all before a hand arrives - was a hard-coded `visible = false` with no way to reach it.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03. STANDALONE THIS ARTIFACT IS A HANDLE. Ignition is bound to the picked_up signal and there is no player during a capture, so every still ever taken of laser_sword shows a 14 cm cylinder and a copper disc inside a 0.95 m bounding box - about 1.8% of the frame at default framing, and the blade the whole piece is about is not in the picture. That is what made this token look unpromotable. The axis is that assumption itself: dark says direction is produced by a body and the object alone is only a grip; pilot says the tool idles, asserting its origin and no further; ghost draws the line full length but cold, geometry without commitment; lit says the vector is a fact about the world rather than about the arm. It is the request_note move - the promotion is about how the thing attaches to the world, not about its size - and the axis doubles as its own fixture, since three of its four values are the only way a blade has ever appeared in a still of this artifact.
dna.declined_second_axis: the blade taper (top_radius = blade_radius * 0.3, a tip on a directed segment) and the copper guard (the boundary where the body stops and the vector begins) are both real arguments and both were refused on measurement grounds. A guard axis is invisible at repose=dark, which is the default the cross-product pairs it with, and the guard is a 58 mm disc on a 950 mm subject - well under a percent of frame, the dilution class. A taper axis moves 2.4 mm against 8 mm at the far end of an 800 mm blade. Either would have produced a finished-looking row of near-identical tiles. One axis that bites is the honest result.
dna.declined_time_domain: swing speed modulating pitch and glow, and the layered hum itself, are the artifact's other live parameters and both are invisible to a still by construction: one is audio, the other depends on a hand moving the object. Named here so a later pass does not rediscover them and declare them.
dna.framing_note: arithmetic, not measured. The AABB is 0.06 x 0.95 x 0.06, diagonal 0.954, and capture_config_sweep fits by DIAGONAL - radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD - which puts a thin tall subject at 2.96 m with a 1.81 m visible height, so the blade covers about 1.8% of the frame area and a real change reads as decoration. 0.65 brings the camera to 1.93 m for a 1.18 m visible height: the 0.95 m sword fills about 80% of frame height with margin, and the blade rises to roughly 4% of frame area. The camera is placed once from the union of all four variants, so the values stay comparable pixel to pixel.

grabbable_line.description: A line segment you grab as one object — pick up anywhere along its length to move it through space. Fixed length, visible endpoints, integer-resistance glitch. Complements the endpoint-first line by teaching whole-before-parts.
grabbable_line.name: Grabbable Line
grabbable_line.qfep_connection: Holding a line whole before decomposing it into endpoints — unity precedes analysis, the body grasps the relation before the mind names the parts.

dna.default: grain=solid - PRESERVES all 16 placements exactly. _build_grain() returns on the first line when grain is solid: no node is added, no property is written, nothing is hidden, and _layout_parts() walks an empty array. The rod, the two endpoint beads, the label, the capsule collider and the glitch loop are the same objects in the same places as before promotion. The metadata read added to _ready only fires when a token carries #grain:, and apply_grid_config now returns without touching anything when the word has not moved - which is what cluster_resolver and curation_station hand it.
dna.was: one unbroken rod with two endpoint beads, in sixteen rooms, with no way to ask what a line is made of - which is the artifact's own truth line ('a line is one thing made of two points') standing as its own contradiction
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03, after the runner refused it as having no turnable knobs. It has exports, but they are a length, a thickness, a radius and four resistance numbers: sizes self-cancel under an AABB-fitted camera and the resistance is a RATE - jitter, a detuning noise loop, haptics - which a still frame cannot photograph. So the sizes and the rate were demoted and the question underneath was built instead. Every rung is standing geometry with no randf in it, and every rung keeps the same +/-line_length/2 envelope, so only the mass inside the silhouette changes.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: grain is taken character for character from cube_scene and prism_block - solid|split|quartered|lattice|shell, the project's one word for how finely a body is made of parts - and the five rungs land exactly on a 1-D body: split is one cut, quartered is three, lattice is eleven on a regular pitch, and shell is the boundary, which for a segment is literally its two endpoints (d[a,b] = {a,b}) as the cube's shell is its twelve edges. The siblings should measure alike on solid->split, which is one gap appearing in one body in both cases.
dna.declined: readout (none|numeral|gradation|lattice), carried by the siblings line, line_interface and xyz_slider_plate. Rungs 0 and 1 fit - this artifact prints '%.2fm' over its midpoint - but rung 3 does not. On line.gd, lattice means the privileged whole numbers on the LENGTH scale, because its resistance fires on the distance between two dragged handles. Here resistance fires on global_position: the whole numbers this artifact privileges are stations in the ROOM, not readings on a rule. Painting a hot collar on the length scale would put the law where it does not live, so the word was declined rather than half-taken.
dna.measurement_risk: a thin subject. The rod is 16 mm across on a 240 mm span while the two endpoint beads are 36 mm and emissive, so the beads own most of the bright pixels and every divided rung changes only the rod. Expect solid->split to read faint by dilution rather than by inertness; crop-recheck before believing it. shell (rod gone, beads only) and lattice (twelve ticks) are the rungs that change the silhouette, and they are the axis's real evidence.

code_evolution_screen.description: Dual-panel VR code viewer — watch code build up stage by stage with parallel thinking narration. Uses SubViewport + RichTextLabel with Catppuccin Mocha syntax highlighting.
code_evolution_screen.name: Code Evolution Screen
code_evolution_screen.qfep_connection: Code as temporal process — each line is a decision, each stage is a conceptual leap. Understanding emerges from watching construction, not reading completion.

PipeLayout.description: High-level pipe network controller with anchor points. Supports glass and drain pipe types. Use PipeLayout#layout:network_name or PipeLayout#pipe_type:glass
PipeLayout.name: PipeLayout
PipeLayout.qfep_connection: Infrastructure as grammar: named anchors and a path list in JSON, committed to glass or drain by the controller. The plumbing exists as a sentence before it exists as volume — the map-equals-data thesis run at pipe scale.

SDFDrawTool.name: SDFDrawTool
SDFDrawTool.qfep_connection: Trigger plus motion drops spheres into a signed-distance field and the marching-cubes mesher reskins the field into clay; there is no eraser, so the sculpture is an unretractable log of everywhere the hand went. Additive-only making — every hesitation and overshoot is kept as form.

aalto_vase.description: Procedural Aalto-style organic vase using Fourier harmonics. Based on Alvar Aalto's Savoy vase (1936).
aalto_vase.name: aalto_vase
aalto_vase.qfep_connection: Flatten the harmonics array to [1.0] and the Savoy silhouette relapses into a plain cylinder; the whole icon lives in three extra cosine coefficients. Authorship survives as a vector short enough to memorize — modernism signed in four floats.

alessi_tree.description: Procedural Alessi-style stacked cone tree with radial stripes. Zigzag lathe form.
alessi_tree.name: alessi_tree
alessi_tree.qfep_connection: Kitsch compresses well: a whole December fits in (tiers, taper, stripe_count, two colors), and the silhouette survives most edits to that vector. The icon's identity turns out to live in a tolerance band, not a shape — flip color_b to teal and it quietly stops being Christmas.

animated_cube.description: Cartesian coordinate system, x y z godot
animated_cube.name: Animated Cube

dna.default: order=ascend, closure=strata - ascend is the shipped chain (vertices at 0.5s, edges at 0.2s, triangles at 0.15s, unchanged timings) and strata is the shipped ending, where nothing is hidden because create_final_mesh() has been commented out for years; the 6 existing placements are byte-for-byte the same animation
dna.was: no exports at all - the sweep refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. Its own @identity names the animation sequence as its critical parameter, but that sequence was welded into a state machine that could only run one direction and could only end one way. order=descend runs the same machine backwards and argues the opposite thesis (a solid DECOMPOSES into faces, edges, corners) instead of the shipped one (dimension ACCUMULATES); order=together removes the dimensional narrative entirely, which is the null case. closure=solid restores the dead create_final_mesh() lineage as a declared choice.

animatedcubebuilder.description: Animated construction sequence that steps from vertices to edges to full cube mesh with grab handles.
animatedcubebuilder.name: animatedcubebuilder
animatedcubebuilder.qfep_connection: The cube assembled in slow motion — vertices, then edges, then faces, with grab handles at each stage. The chapter's core sentence played as animation: everything from nothing, watched happening, the eight corners of the grid's own unit born one construction step at a time.

arch.description: Architectural arch with curved top and pillars
arch.name: Arch
arch.qfep_connection: Two rectangular pillars and a twelve-segment half-circle: the first primitive whose form is a job — carrying weight across an absence. The curve is straight segments agreeing to look continuous, so the smoothness and the implied strength are both resolution effects the eye ratifies.

array_rotate.description: Array + Rotate. rotation[i] = i Ã— angle. The fan/wheel: cumulative rotation around axis.
array_rotate.name: array_rotate
array_rotate.qfep_connection: rotation[i] = i × 30° over twelve copies: the wheel closes only because count and angle conspire to reach exactly 360. The fan is modular arithmetic wearing boxes — change either number and the circle gapes or overlaps, and the 'shape' confesses it was a coincidence of parameters.

array_scale.description: Array + Scale. scale[i] = factor^i. The nest: cumulative scaling (telescoping).
array_scale.name: array_scale
array_scale.qfep_connection: scale[i] = 0.75^i stacks eight plates into a ziggurat that converges toward a point it will never reach — a geometric series you can stand next to. Exponential decay staged as furniture, with the limit left honestly unbuilt.

array_translate.description: Array + Translate. position[i] = i Ã— offset. The staircase: cumulative translation.
array_translate.name: array_translate
array_translate.qfep_connection: position[i] = i × offset — the staircase is not designed but secreted, the residue of one instruction that never varies. Climbability turns out to be a property of a multiplication.

array_visualizer.description: Interactive tool for visualizing array structures
array_visualizer.name: Array Visualizer
array_visualizer.qfep_connection: The row never changes; only the lit head moves along it, and the readout names i and a[i] as two separate terms so the pointer and the contents cannot be mistaken for one thing. That gap between a place and what is currently in it is where every off-by-one, every hash collision and every sorted-in-place lie actually lives.

arrow.name: arrow
arrow.qfep_connection: The same script as the coordinate axis with show_ticks switched off: strip the ruler marks and a line stops measuring and starts pointing. Direction is what remains of a coordinate when you delete its scale.

bigframe.description: Hollow rectangular beam with configurable dimensions
bigframe.name: bigframe
bigframe.qfep_connection: A hollow rectangular beam — the quad given thickness and a window. The primitive becoming architecture: a frame is a shape that has decided what to leave out, enclosure defined by its hole.

bipyramid.description: Double-ended pyramid primitive formed by mirrored pyramid faces.
bipyramid.name: bipyramid
bipyramid.qfep_connection: Two triangle fans meet at a square the mesh never draws: the base becomes interior the instant it is shared, and reflection erases the very seam it reflects across. The one face both halves agree on is exactly the face that vanishes.

bucket_of_tulips.description: A charming metal bucket filled with colorful tulips, bringing natural beauty and algorithmic growth patterns to the laboratory space
bucket_of_tulips.name: Bucket of Tulips

capsule.description: Grid-shaded capsule primitive with glowing wireframe overlay.
capsule.name: capsule
capsule.qfep_connection: A cylinder that rounded its ends — the primitive of the *organic*, the shape a body or a pill takes when it refuses corners. Grid-shaded with a glowing wireframe, it holds both codes at once: the lattice underneath, the smoothness on top.

capsule_radials_rings.description: Configurable capsule with radial segments and rings. Usage: capsule_radials_rings:90:1:#radial:6#rings:3 for 6 radial segments and 3 rings.
capsule_radials_rings.name: Capsule Radials Rings

dna.default: cross_section=octagonal (radial_segments=8), caps=domed (rings=4) - the two literals capsule_radials_rings.gd and capsule_radials_rings.tscn have always authored, so the 15 placements are unchanged. The named axes only speak where the NUMERIC path was silent: _radial_explicit / _rings_explicit are set by #config, #radial, #rings and set_capsule_params, and the raw counts win. That matters here more than anywhere - 18 of this token's placements already pass #radial:3 or #radial:7 with #rings:3, and every one of them keeps its exact number.
dna.was: radial_segments=8 and rings=4 were this artifact's own declared critical_parameter, reachable only as bare integers through a #radial/#rings token with no vocabulary and no registry declaration. The exports existed; nothing named what they ARGUE.
dna.note: THIS IS NOT A RESOLUTION AXIS and the corpus proved it before the code did: maps were already placing this token at radial_segments=3, which is not a rough capsule but a triangular prism with a tent at each end - at 4 a square beam, at 6 a hexagonal barrel. It does not read as 'a capsule, less smooth' until somewhere around 12, which is why round is 24 and not 12. The artifact's own qfep_connection says it: 'turn the dial down and the body becomes a barrel.' A barrel is a different object. caps is the second constituent, and it argues with the artifact's own truth line - 'the capsule is the physicist's preferred solid, its hemispherical ends are differentiable at all points'. Godot spends rings on the hemispheres, so at rings=1 each hemisphere collapses to one band from equator to pole, i.e. a CONE with an apex: the exact point where the derivative does not exist. The truth line is not a property of capsules, it is a property of capsules built with enough rings, and nothing in the family could say so until now.
dna.family: does not collide with the sibling capsule token in the same directory, whose facture axis (cast|facet|armature|section|wear) asks how a made body is PRESENTED and whose header explicitly declares its own 5 segments and 5 rings legacy and never written to. The segment question was left vacant for this token; it takes it. The word resolution was considered and refused: sphere_mid owns it for the amount of a budget, and the honest reading here is identity of a solid, not amount of a budget.
dna.corpus_note: CLAUDE.md records a KNOWN GAP - 'exactly ONE map (Artist_Readymades, six request_note tokens) places any artifact at a non-default value.' That is now false in this token's favour: capsule_radials_rings has 18 live placements at #radial:3 / #radial:7. Worth correcting, because it is the only other place in the corpus where a player has ever met a variant.

capsule_radials_rings.qfep_connection: The capsule with its resolution exposed — radial segments and rings you can set. The reminder that every smooth thing here is secretly faceted, curvature a lie told convincingly by enough flat pieces. Turn the dial down and the body becomes a barrel.

capsules.name: capsules
capsules.qfep_connection: A police lineup of capsules whose only variable is mesh resolution — 4, 5, 6 radial segments beside a 32-ring 'smooth' one. Smoothness stands in the row as just another head-count: the number past which the eye gives up counting.

cavetest.name: cavetest
cavetest.qfep_connection: Ten orbs land on the cave's inner wall and each flips a seeded coin: union or subtraction, bump or hollow. The interior you walk through is the ledger of those ten decisions — growth and excavation are the same gesture with one operation bit flipped.

chaos_attractor.description: Visualization of chaotic systems and strange attractors
chaos_attractor.name: Chaos Attractor
chaos_attractor.qfep_connection: lambda_edge: strange attractors traced live — deterministic rules whose futures diverge from any measurable present. The room where F = ma stops promising prediction.

combine_capsule.description: Arranges capsule meshes in a matrix while iterating through height and radial segment combinations.
combine_capsule.name: combine_capsule
combine_capsule.qfep_connection: Height stretches the middle while segments sharpen the skin: one axis measures the world, the other measures how coarsely you agreed to describe it. The sweep lays both kinds of number side by side and lets neither pretend to be the other.

dna.default: taxonomy=ladder, refinement=linear - the legacy build statement for statement. `ladder` returns Vector3(0, 0, i * spacing), the same float in the same place as the original loop, and `linear` returns rings = start + i and ring_segments = start + 2i, the same two integers in the same order. All 4 existing placements are unchanged, and no map carries a #taxonomy: or #refinement: token today.
dna.was: the `taxonomy` axis was written into combine_portals.gd in an earlier pass and NEVER DECLARED here, so the sweep read the token as having no turnable knobs and refused it - a live axis invisible to every tool that reads the registry. Declared now by derivation from the @export_enum, not by transcription. `refinement` is new: rings = start + i and ring_segments = start + 2i were a statement written once, so a corridor whose own truth line is 'you choose how many polygons' could not be asked to choose differently.
dna.note: the two axes are a control pair and are strictly orthogonal in code - _taxonomy_offset touches only transform.origin and never a mesh, _refined_wires touches only rings/ring_segments and never a position. taxonomy varies WHERE the family stands with the meshes held; refinement varies WHAT the meshes are with the arrangement held. `inverted` is the built-in null: it is the same twenty meshes as `linear` in reverse order, so an identical multiset in a different direction, and if it does not read differently in a still then the coarse-to-fine story was never legible. `fixed` is the other null - twenty identical coarse rings, the corridor with its ladder removed.
dna.kin: `taxonomy` with exactly table/ladder/stack/heap is the folder's word, shared character for character with combine_sphere, combine_capsule, math_objects and math_objects_gallery - one grammar for the whole parameter-sweep family, so a room holding several of them cannot have two arguing taxonomy and a third arguing corridor. Note the default differs from its siblings: combine_sphere and combine_capsule ship at `table` because they were authored as lattices, and this one ships at `ladder` because it was authored as a ninety-metre corridor. `refinement` is a new word - the nearest neighbour is sphere_low's `grain` (meridian/parallel/even), but grain asks WHERE one object's budget goes and this asks HOW a series' budget grows, which is a different question and so takes a different word.
dna.framing_note: spine_hints() already tags this artifact `oversized` and `corridor_incompatible` because `ladder` runs ~90 m along +Z, and that is exactly the pivot of the taxonomy axis: it is the one value you cannot see all of from anywhere, and table/stack/heap are the same twenty rings brought into a single view. A sweep tile of `ladder` will therefore read as a receding tunnel rather than a chart, which is the argument, not a capture fault.
dna.guard: apply_grid_config is gated per key AND on _ready having resolved the base torus - it returns early when neither key is present, when the value is unrecognised, when the value already matches, and when _base_portal/_base_mesh are still null. So a token carrying only other keys, or a config applied before the node enters the tree, cannot rebuild a corridor that is already standing.

combine_portals.description: Duplicates a base torus to form a tunnel of portals that grow denser down the hallway.
combine_portals.name: combine_portals
combine_portals.qfep_connection: One torus duplicated down a hall, denser as it recedes — the primitive caught in the act of becoming a corridor. Repetition with a gradient: how a single ring, told to multiply toward a vanishing point, manufactures depth out of nothing but its own copies.

combine_primitives.description: Shows four procedural walled-cube modules (cylinder, plane, sphere, torus) side by side for layout inspection.
combine_primitives.name: combine_primitives
combine_primitives.qfep_connection: Four nodes named cylinder, plane, sphere, and torus all instance the identical walled-cube scene — the names are aspiration, the geometry never differentiates. A layout rig where the labels promise a taxonomy the mesh refuses to deliver.

combine_sphere.description: Builds a grid of spheres varying ring and radial segment settings with optional hemisphere alternation.
combine_sphere.name: combine_sphere
combine_sphere.qfep_connection: A walkable table of one decision: every rings-by-segments pair gets its own labelled ball, the coarse ones reading as faceted gems, the fine ones as smooth. A sphere shown to be a resolution you choose with your eyes.

combine_torus.description: Generates a gradient-colored grid of torus meshes sweeping through ring and segment counts.
combine_torus.name: combine_torus
combine_torus.qfep_connection: Smoothness is exposed as a spend: the same donut appears 121 times, each surface painted with exactly the ring and segment counts that drew it, from faceted hoop to soft torus. The ideal surface never shows up — only differently priced approximations of it, all on one table.

combo_cube_visual.description: A visual-only cube that moves, rotates, and scales simultaneously (Not a pickup).
combo_cube_visual.name: Transformation Rotation Scale Cube
combo_cube_visual.qfep_connection: Bob, spin, and a 1.8x breathing scale run as three sibling scripts on one cube, transformation by stacking rather than choreography — no script knows the others exist. And it is explicitly not a pickup: all that liveliness is display, motion the hand is refused.

concept_synthesizer.description: Device for synthesizing abstract concepts into tangible forms
concept_synthesizer.name: Concept Synthesizer
concept_synthesizer.registry_note: RETIRED 2026-07-29 (build-or-retire triage): Registered scene is an empty stub and no implementation exists anywhere in the repo.

coordinate_axes_xy.description: Displays orthogonal X/Y line modules with floating labels for quick planar orientation.
coordinate_axes_xy.name: coordinate_axes_xy
coordinate_axes_xy.qfep_connection: Y is not its own thing: it is the X axis instanced a second time and rotated 90 degrees, with billboard letters doing the work of keeping two identical arrows distinct. Orthogonality here is a transform plus a label — the plane's second dimension is a reuse.

coordinate_readout.description: One axis of the grab point's position as a wall work — x = 1.24 on a dark panel, fed live by CoordinateSystem3M through the ada_coordinate_readout group.
coordinate_readout.name: coordinate_readout

coordinate_lines.description: Orthogonal vertical and horizontal line modules forming a coordinate axis crosshair.
coordinate_lines.name: coordinate_lines
coordinate_lines.qfep_connection: Two copies of the same static line, one laid on its side, meeting at origin: the crosshair before it has earned arrowheads or letters. Axes at the stage where they are still only incidence — not yet direction, not yet name.

cross_line_puzzle.description: Interactive puzzle: drag line endpoints to form an X cross from two horizontal lines. Tag syntax: cross_line_puzzle:rot:ytrans:scale#tagname:action (e.g., cross_line_puzzle:0:0:1#fillhole:reveal triggers 'reveal' action on all nodes tagged 'fillhole' when solved)
cross_line_puzzle.name: Cross Line Puzzle

dna.default: frame=diagonal, stock=stacked - diagonal hands back the four shipped corner literals (0,0.2,-0.2), (0,-0.2,0.2), (0,-0.2,-0.2), (0,0.2,0.2) verbatim instead of re-deriving them, and stacked returns the two parallel lines at x=0.2, y=-0.25/-0.4 verbatim, so every existing placement (4 map tokens, incl. the tagged one in Point_Line_Context) opens in exactly the layout it had before
dna.was: no exports of its own: four target corners and two starting segments written as literal arrays in _init(), and no apply_grid_config(). The subclass differs from plus_line_puzzle ONLY in those corner literals - both call FormConstraint.cross_constraints() - so the X was shipped as if it were a different figure when it is the same relation at a different angle
dna.note: frame is the argument axis: upright turns the same four points 45 degrees so the finished figure is a plus, made from the same two lines under the same perpendicular + intersect-at-centres test, and oblique parks them 20 degrees off so neither name is available and only the relation is left. stock is the family word shared with plus_line_puzzle (same three layouts, same coordinates) and with triangle_line_puzzle (same word, its own three values) - what the unassembled parts give away before you touch them. Script confirmed on the .tscn ROOT node (CrossLinePuzzle), not on a child, so both axes are reachable from a map token.

cross_line_puzzle.qfep_connection: Two draggable lines, four shared snap targets, and a solution accepted only when the constraints PERPENDICULAR and INTERSECT_CENTER both hold: the X is not a picture to copy but a predicate to satisfy, and satisfying it can fire actions on any node tagged to listen.

cross_lines.description: Pair of line modules rotated into an X to demonstrate intersecting lines.
cross_lines.name: cross_lines
cross_lines.qfep_connection: Origin here is not placed but produced: two diagonals are configured independently and the center point exists only as their agreement. Nudge either endpoint and the location migrates — a point as the outcome of negotiation rather than an address.

crystal.description: Procedurally built quartz-style crystal with layered facets.
crystal.name: crystal
crystal.qfep_connection: Six-fold symmetry run up an axis with a radius that swells then tapers (0.8, 0.9, 0.6) — mineral growth as a for-loop with a profile. The unused crystal_type variable ('quartz', 'amethyst', 'emerald') is the honest part: the names are marketing, the geometry only ever knew rings and radii.

crystalcluster.description: Cluster of scaled crystals arranged with deterministic offsets.
crystalcluster.name: crystalcluster
crystalcluster.qfep_connection: Five crystals scattered by dice loaded to land identically every run — rng.seed = i × 42 — so the cluster performs geological accident while being fully scripted. Disorder as a look the code wears, not a property it has.

cube.description: Static cube with grid shader and collider, used as a baseline geometric primitive.
cube.name: cube
cube.qfep_connection: Half-edge 0.5, so the default body is exactly one grid cell: the primitive and the system that places it agree on a unit, and apply_grid_config is the amendment clause of that treaty.

cube_lines.name: cube_lines
cube_lines.qfep_connection: Twelve thin lines and no faces: the cube reduced to its adjacency, an inventory of edges showing the volume was always an inference the eye supplies.

dna.default: disclosure=frame, coding=uniform - all twelve edges drawn at thickness 0.008 in Color(0.4, 0.8, 1.0), which is the exact shipped call, so the 3 existing placements render byte for byte as before
dna.was: twelve edges, one blue, always - the registry's own line about the volume being an inference the eye supplies was stated at only one volume of speech and so could not be argued with
dna.note: the twelve edge positions are identical for every value of both axes; disclosure only decides which edges are drawn, coding only their tint. Nothing is added to the scene and nothing moves.

dna.default: warning=none is the export default and the `_:` branch of _build_warning, which adds no node at all. All 9 placements are unchanged: Corridor_Random_Game, MindMap_Primitives, Room_Random_Game and Random_Game_* x5 plus TemplateMap_Descent13, of which six carry the long #mode:field#field_size:8x8#... chain and none of the nine passes a `warning` key. _build_warning runs LAST in _ready, after _setup_spawner, _find_player and activate_spawner, so MeshInstance3D, SpawnTimer, SpawnPoint, WarningParticles, SpawnSound, WarningSound and Label3D all keep their child indices. configure() reads the key only when it is PRESENT and names a legal value DIFFERENT from the one already standing, which matters because six of the nine send a dozen field_* keys on every load and must not tear the dressing down. An unrecognised word keeps the current value: a typo must not silently uncage a live hazard.
dna.was: BROKEN, and not by omission of a genome. The axis, its allow-list, its five-rung doc block, the field_seed pin and the idle_still fixture flag were already in CubeSpawner.gd from an earlier pass, and _ready and configure both CALLED _build_warning() — a function that existed nowhere in the script. In GDScript 4 that is a resolution error at parse time, so the script did not load and cube_projectile_spawner rendered nothing in any of its nine rooms. The declaration gate cannot catch this class: the export is real and its values are real, and it is the builder that is absent (dna_specimen's fault one step further along). The whole of this pass is the five builders, the bounds reader, the cover-height reader and this declaration. Found by scanning every .gd in b0428de74 'rescue(dna): 35 promotions that were written and never committed' for self-calls with no definition; the other eight hits were inherited helpers or a comment, so this is the rescue's only casualty.
dna.note: warning is kaleidocycle_enemy's word and its five values character for character — miura_crawler, scissor_stalker, kresling_spire, origami_droideka, path_cube, path_pyramid, path_wedge and force_vortex already ask it, and a room cannot coherently cage its crawlers and leave the thing that shoots at them unannounced. The colours, the `hazard_warning` group and the four builders are that artifact's, resized from this one's own AABB rather than copied at its scale, so the family photographs as one apparatus at eight sizes. The sharpest case in the family for its own reason: the spawner is not the danger, it is the SOURCE of the danger, and between two firings it is a box on the floor doing nothing at all — so what the room says about a currently idle box is not a property of the box. stain is legible only from inside the field of fire; beacon is the only rung that reaches you at the doorway; shroud reaches up past the placard at y 1.5 so the machine and its own hazard sign go under the canvas together, because a wrap that left the sign legible would not be a wrap. APPEARANCE ONLY: spawn_interval, projectile_speed, max_projectiles, target_prediction, spawn_mode and every field_* number are byte-identical across all five, and no value adds or removes a collider. A hazard that hides itself is not a gentler hazard.
dna.fixture_note: idle_still is a fixture and NOT an axis. auto_start is true, so activate_spawner runs in _ready and starts both a looping 0.5 s pulse tween on the housing and the 50-particle warning plume; a still 1.1 s in catches the box at an arbitrary scale between 1.0 and 1.2 and the plume at an arbitrary density, which is per-variant noise on top of the axis. idle_still skips both and is declared as the STRING "true" on purpose — the export is untyped for exactly this reason, since a typed bool rejects a fixture string before _ready and does it silently. field_seed is not in the fixture because it is not reachable in a still: spawn_mode defaults to FORWARD, which never draws from _rng, and the first projectile is due at t=6.0 s against a 1.1 s settle, so no capture of the default has a projectile in it at all.
dna.declined: spawn_interval, projectile_speed, fall_min/fall_max and jitter_interval were all considered and refused: a rate and a duration are invisible to a single frame, which is the info_board fault. spawn_mode = forward|falling_field is real, argues something (a shot aimed at you versus weather that does not know you are there) and is ALREADY reachable from a map token via configure()'s `mode` key — but the difference lives entirely in cubes that do not exist until t=6.0 s, so a still of the two modes is the same red box twice.

cube_projectile_spawner.description: Timed hazard that spawns projectile cubes, leads the target, and fires warning effects before launch.
cube_projectile_spawner.name: cube_projectile_spawner
cube_projectile_spawner.qfep_connection: It does not shoot at you, it shoots at where its model says you will be: target_prediction leads the player's velocity before every launch. Being hunted here means being forecast, with the warning glow as the only courtesy.

cube_scene.capacity: TEST how cubes can split, snap, scale, and recombine while remaining the basic reference primitive.
cube_scene.description: A configurable cube scene used as reference geometry across the project. Its variants can be grabbed, scaled, subdivided, snapped, or augmented, but the cube remains the stable primitive beneath those state changes. That makes it ideal for seeing what a transformation preserves and what it alters. In the transformation sequence it functions as the baseline form against which other changes read clearly.
interactions: grab cube variants and move them through space
compare scaled, subdivided, and snapped cube behaviors
attach or detach auxiliary utilities where present
use the cube as a baseline reference for other transformed forms
cube_scene.name: Basic Cube Scene
cube_scene.qfep_connection: Transformation changes S while the cube serves as the invariant reference body. Because the base form is so legible, every modification becomes easy to compare against it.

dna.default: grain=solid - the shipped code path, so existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: a cube shipped as one undivided block, so the question of what a cube is made of could not be asked of it
dna.note: declared by hand 2026-07-29 — the axis was already in the script and the registry had never been told, so the sweep could not reach it

cube_scene_drag_points.name: cube_scene_drag_points
cube_scene_drag_points.qfep_connection: Eight grab spheres, one per corner, and the cube turns out to be a treaty among vertices: drag one and the faces re-triangulate around your decision. Rigidity revealed as a default, not a property.

dna.default: handles=corners, triangulation=fixed - all eight spheres live and every quad split on the author's a-c diagonal, which is the exact historical triangle list, so all 6 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: no axes of its own: the treaty was hard-coded to eight signatories in a for i in range(8), and each face carried a fixed seam written out twice as a literal triangle list in create_vr_cube() and update_cube_mesh()
dna.note: triangulation is DEFORMATION-VISIBLE ONLY - at rest the cube is square and both diagonals are equal, so a still capture of an untouched cube scores the two modes identical. The axis bites when a corner is dragged, which a still cannot show; judge it from a deformed frame or not at all.

cube_with_shader.description: Cartesian coordinate system, x y z godot
cube_with_shader.name: Cube with shader
cube_with_shader.qfep_connection: The mesh never moves; only shader uniforms breathe — emission hue cycles, grid lines pulse wide and narrow. Change confined entirely to the skin while the geometry holds still: E_flux in appearance, F_order untouched underneath.

cylinder.description: Basic grid-lined cylinder primitive for quick scale checks.
cylinder.name: cylinder
cylinder.qfep_connection: Roundness is a token in map_data: #config:4 lands a square prism, #config:16 a smooth column, the same lookup name resolving to different degrees of the circle-lie. The map, not the mesh, decides how hard this primitive pretends to be continuous.

cylinder_low.description: Low poly cylinder with 8 radial segments showing faceted structure.
cylinder_low.name: cylinder_low
cylinder_low.qfep_connection: Eight radial segments, hard-coded: an octagon asking to be read as a circle. Held at this resolution not from thrift but as a specimen — the approximation pinned open one step before the eye would forgive it.

cylinder_mid.description: Medium poly cylinder with 16 radial segments for smooth curves.
cylinder_mid.name: cylinder_mid
cylinder_mid.qfep_connection: Identical radius and height to its low-poly sibling, only radial_segments doubled to sixteen: the pair stages resolution as the sole variable. Whatever difference you perceive between them is pure sampling rate — the cylinder itself appears in neither.

cylinder_radials_rings.description: Configurable cylinder with radial segments and rings. Usage: cylinder_radials_rings:90:1:#config:12:8 for 12 radial segments and 8 rings.
cylinder_radials_rings.name: Cylinder Radials Rings
cylinder_radials_rings.qfep_connection: The map itself gets a vote on how round this is: '#config:12:8' reaches through the grid layer to set radial_segments, so 'cylinder' names a range running from square prism to smooth column. Roundness as a negotiable quantity rather than a shape.

dgrid.description: Standing perspective grid frame inspired by Albrecht DÃ¼rer. Use dgrid:90:1:1#config:10:10 for 10x10 grid.
dgrid.name: DÃ¼rer Grid
dgrid.qfep_connection: Dürer's perspective frame standing in the room — the drafting instrument that taught the Renaissance to project three dimensions onto two. The primitive of *seeing*: before you can build space you must agree how to depict it, and this grid is that agreement made in wood.

diamond.description: Faceted diamond mesh generated with grid shading for highlights.
diamond.name: diamond
diamond.qfep_connection: An octahedron with unequal poles — apex pulled to 0.6 while the base stops at −0.4 — so the gem is the regular solid plus one deliberate injustice along its axis. Preciousness is staged by breaking the symmetry, not by keeping it.

diamonds.description: Stacks rotating solids into a twisting tower. DNA: twist_rule selects HOW the angle accumulates up the stack (linear=the helix, fixed=no accumulation, alternating=braid between two orientations, accelerating=same total twist reached superlinearly); unit selects which solid the rule acts on. Config: #twist_rule:fixed#unit:tetrahedron

dna.default: twist_rule=linear, unit=octahedron - the exact pre-promotion construction (rotation.y = rotation_offset * i on stacked octahedron.tscn), so the 11 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: the artifact's own truth statement says the RULE is more fundamental than the result, and the rule was the one thing hard-coded: rotation_offset * i, linear accumulation, stated once and never varied. The four exports it did have (unit_count, unit_size, unit_height, rotation_offset) only changed how big the same claim was, which is why the sweep read it as having no turnable knobs.
dna.note: The two axes are a control pair: twist_rule varies the rule with the unit held, unit varies the unit with the rule held. fixed is the null hypothesis the docstring already named — every unit turned by the same amount, no accumulation, no helix. accelerating reaches the same total twist at the top as linear by a different path, so the endpoints agree and the form does not.

diamonds.name: diamonds
diamonds.qfep_connection: Octahedra stacked and rotated into a twisting tower — the single primitive multiplied into sculpture. The chapter's quiet thesis made ornamental: give one regular solid a rule for repeating and it grows a spire nobody carved.

dimension_lens.name: Dimension Lens
dimension_lens.registry_note: RETIRED 2026-07-29 (build-or-retire triage): Registered scene is an empty stub and no implementation exists anywhere in the repo.

dodecahedron.description: Procedural dodecahedron solid using grid material.
dodecahedron.name: dodecahedron
dodecahedron.qfep_connection: The cosmos-solid is built from twenty addresses that mix cube corners with golden-ratio points — PHI is not symbolism here, it is the literal coordinate. And it renders only by concession: each irreducible pentagon is fan-cut into triangles because the GPU accepts no other polygon.

dome.description: Half-sphere primitive produced by boolean subtraction — used as reference geometry for enclosures and shelters.
dome.name: dome
dome.qfep_connection: A half-sphere cut from a solid by boolean subtraction — reference geometry for enclosure, the simplest roof. In the procedural rooms it stands as the authored control against which the grown forms are measured: this is what shape looks like when someone *drew* it, so you can feel how different the grown ones are.

doublestick.name: doublestick
doublestick.qfep_connection: A line that exists only as a relation: the cylinder is rebuilt sixty times a second between ForceOne and ForceTwo, and moving either endpoint redraws the connection. The segment owns no position of its own.

draw_dot.description: sample(hand_position) → ImmediateMesh trail — the hand writes points in 3D space
draw_dot.name: draw_dot
draw_dot.qfep_connection: The hand becomes an instrument that leaves evidence: sampled positions accumulate into a trail, and six meters of accrued drawing throws the unlock. A curve confessed as dense point samples, with a door listening to how far you have moved.

dna.default: retention=none - NOTHING IN THIS ARTIFACT'S CODE CHANGED. The axis was already exported, already implemented and already reachable; the promotion is the declaration and a fix to the checker that could not see it. _ready calls super._ready(), which reaches _ret_read_config() and _ret_build() at the end of the parent's body, and "none" is the first case of that match and builds no record at all. MEASURED, not assumed: 8 mentions across 7 map files, not the 4 the promotion brief carried, by two reach-paths - bare tokens in WaveFunctions_Pendulum and its three parts, and three curation_station collections (Corridor_Point_One, Corridor_WaveFunctions_Pendulum, Curation_Bay_wavefunctions_3) whose #layout and #with_wall / #with_pillars / #with_barrier flags belong to the station and not to this artifact. None carries a retention key, and the inherited apply_grid_config returns on its first line unless a config actually carries one.
dna.was: refused by the runner as NO TURNABLE KNOBS, and that refusal was a fact about a line-oriented parser rather than about the artifact. This file is 92 lines beginning `extends "res://commons/primitives/point/draw_dot.gd"`, and its whole standing genome - the retention export, the RETENTIONS allow-list, the five _ret_* builders, the gated apply_grid_config - is the parent's. GDScript forbids redeclaring an inherited member, so the child cannot restate it and should not: the honest fix was to teach tools/check_dna_declarations.py to follow `extends "res://..."`, which it now does, and which closes the same gap for any artifact whose axis lives one class up.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: draw_dot (the parent script), draw_triangle_faces, grab_sphere_point_snap, interactive_point_origin_force, player_trace, mystic_writing_pad, oscillation_controlled_cube - `retention` with the same five values in the same order and the same default. Here it is inherited rather than copied, so the sibling cannot drift: it is literally the same code.
dna.declined: time_axis_speed, sample_interval and lock_origin_on_ready - this file's own three exports, and all three declined. The first two are a rate and an interval, which one still cannot tell apart; that is the info_board result exactly. The third is invisible by construction. And the live trace itself is declined as a subject: with no player and no grab, the draw sphere never moves, so every sample lands on the same point and the +Z push draws them into a straight 0.2 m line - a degenerate figure that is the same figure at every value. The standing, photographable record in the reference frame is the parent's retention record, which is why that is the axis and the time axis is not.
dna.still_note: the record is built once in _ready inside the 0.5 m reference frame and never moves, so a still is a complete account of it. The child's _process advances the live trail along +Z but touches no part of the record.

draw_dot_time_domain.description: Draw dot with time-domain trace along +Z.
draw_dot_time_domain.name: draw_dot_time_domain
draw_dot_time_domain.qfep_connection: oscillation: a dot that draws its own history — motion smeared into a time-domain trace; the simplest possible oscilloscope.

draw_triangle_faces.description: fan_triangulate(loop) → colored mesh face — closed point loops become surfaces
draw_triangle_faces.name: draw_triangle_faces
draw_triangle_faces.qfep_connection: fan_triangulate(loop) → a colored surface: the moment a closed loop of points stops being an outline and becomes a face you could stand on. The bridge from edge to skin — how everything solid in this project is, underneath, triangles agreeing to be a plane.

dynamic_rock.description: Single procedural rock with gravity enabled - falls naturally with physics
dynamic_rock.name: Dynamic Rock
dynamic_rock.qfep_connection: The craggy mesh is noise-deformed icosphere theatre, but the physics engine only ever touches the 0.3m sphere collider underneath. What falls is a perfect ball; what we watch fall is a rock — individuality rendered as skin over an interchangeable body.

editable_bezier.description: Cubic Bezier curve editor. 4 control points: P0-P1 defines start tangent, P2-P3 defines end tangent. Shows tangent handles.
editable_bezier.name: editable_bezier
editable_bezier.qfep_connection: Two of the four points you hold, the curve refuses to visit — Bézier reads P1 and P2 as pull, never as fact, and the grey tangent lines are the drawn diagram of that partial trust. Authority over a shape can be exercised without ever being touched by it.

editable_catmull_rom.description: Catmull-Rom spline editor. Curve passes through all control points. More intuitive for freeform drawing.
editable_catmull_rom.name: editable_catmull_rom
editable_catmull_rom.qfep_connection: The spline that honors every point it is given — and pays for that honesty by inventing phantoms, mirroring points beyond both ends so the real endpoints have somewhere to come from. Total inclusion needs fictions at the border.

editable_curve.description: Interactive curve with grabbable control points. Supports Bezier, Catmull-Rom, and linear modes. Extends the trace concept: deliberate construction over recorded gesture.
editable_curve.name: editable_curve
editable_curve.qfep_connection: The same four grabbable spheres yield three different shapes depending on which basis function is asked to believe them — interpolation exposed as jurisprudence, not fact. And the drawn result is a 32-segment polyline: even the chosen law reaches the eye already sampled.

elevator_platform.description: Platform that slides up/down on Y axis. Teaches vertical translation with grid snapping to floor levels.
elevator_platform.name: Elevator Platform
elevator_platform.qfep_connection: A floor that is also a handle: grabbable like any pickable but permitted only Y, gravity zeroed, snap_to_grid quantizing height to the grid's one-meter floors. Elevation is not climbed here but selected — vertical translation with the continuum confiscated.

falling_cube.description: Simple falling cube for physics testing
falling_cube.name: Falling Cube
falling_cube.qfep_connection: Named cube, drawn as a four-segment sphere, colliding as a box — three descriptions of one body, and the physics engine reads only the third. Falling is the single thing it does, and it does that with no script at all: gravity as the one behavior that never needed authoring.

folded_strip.description: triangle_strip(24) — alternating-height vertices forming a pleated ribbon of connected faces
folded_strip.name: 1.2: folded_strip
folded_strip.qfep_connection: triangle_strip(24) — a pleated ribbon of alternating heights, faces sharing edges down its length. The most economical surface in the project: maximum face from minimum vertex, the primitive of the fold that the softbody and creature chapters will later make move.

foldedpaper.description: Accordion-style folded paper mesh with editable top/base control points and multiple fold reset modes.
foldedpaper.name: 1.2: A foldedpaper
foldedpaper.qfep_connection: The sheet is nothing but stretched skin between two rows of grabbable marbles — move one and SurfaceTool re-sews the paper around your decision. The accordion arrives pre-pleated at 70%: the fold is mostly decided before the first hand touches it.

folding_cube.description: Animated cube net folding into 3D cube. Shows how 6 connected squares become a volume. Cross net with hinge animation.
folding_cube.name: folding_cube
folding_cube.qfep_connection: Six squares hinge from cross to closed volume, then the finished cube is handed to gravity and a fresh flat net appears in its place — the floor slowly filling with identical cubes, each one a timestamp of the same irreversible collapse from 2D possibility into 3D fact.

folding_cube_interactive.description: Interactive folding cube. Grab the handle to manually fold/unfold. Snaps to flat or folded state on release.
folding_cube_interactive.name: folding_cube_interactive
folding_cube_interactive.qfep_connection: Handle height IS fold progress — an inverse_lerp puts topology in the wrist, and the cube unfolds exactly as far as you lower your hand. But release, and the 0.5 threshold decides for you: the continuum you were scrubbing snaps to flat or folded the moment the grip ends.

dna.default: recession=nested - a no-op. `nested` has no case in the match block: it IS the arrangement computed above it, line for line what shipped (frame_progress from the clock, scale = pow(scale_ratio, p * frame_count), z = z_base_offset - p * 4.5, alpha 0.9 -> 0.3), and _ready's new set_process(recession == 'nested') resolves to set_process(true) on an object that was already processing. apply_grid_config returns immediately unless a config actually names 'recession' and names something different. All 28 placements (29 tokens across 29 maps by direct count) pass no config at all, so every one of them animates exactly as before - same MultiMesh, same instance count, same AABB, same auto-ground lift.
dna.was: seven exports and not one of them an argument: frame_width, frame_height, frame_count, frame_thickness, cycle_duration, scale_ratio, z_base_offset, frame_color. Every one is a rate, a size or a colour - a map could make the fold faster, bigger or bluer, and could not make it say anything else. Two of them (cycle_duration, and scale_ratio only through the animation) are time-domain, which is why this loop's one-still-per-value evidence would have photographed six identical nests at six speeds. That is the info_board mistake, and it is what 'no turnable knobs' was actually reporting: there were knobs, and none of them turned toward a different claim.
dna.note: The axis is the file's own truth line made switchable. 'The past does not vanish - it recedes, each moment nesting inside the one that follows' is a CLAIM about the shape of time, and the artifact could only ever assert it. `abreast` stages the figure the nesting was built to refuse (succession without containment: the timeline, every moment the same size, none inside another). `strata` stages the third figure (deposition: the past underneath rather than behind, newest layer on top). `collapsed` drives the nest to its own limit - ten frames on the innermost term, one small dim rectangle with nothing legible behind it. Age still fades by index in all four, so what changes between the tiles is the arrangement and only the arrangement.
dna.kin: `fold` was considered and declined. polyhedron_nets_cube took it two batches ago for animated|closed|hinged|flat, and the value list cannot transfer: there is no hinge in this object and nothing closes into a solid, so `hinged` and `closed` would be values named after a mechanism the artifact does not have. Taking the word without its answers is the dishonest half of a shared vocabulary, so the word here is the file's own subject - recession - with its own four values. `posture` (qfep_formula_3d: line|stack|arc|ring) was declined for the same reason in reverse: it asks how terms are laid out, and this asks what shape TIME takes, which is not a layout question even though it is answered with a layout.
dna.harness_note: The subject is a MultiMeshInstance3D, which the capture's _get_combined_aabb does handle (unlike the MeshInstance3D-only case in CLAUDE.md) - but the frames sit at z = -8.0 to -12.5 with the node origin at 0, so the fitted AABB is a long box whose centre is ten metres from the origin. Check the first tile before trusting a low bite number, and reach for dna.framing rather than for a `layers = 0` anchor: grounding measures the same AABB, so an anchor would move all 28 shipped placements. `strata` stacks UPWARD from the nested base plane on purpose, so its min_y matches nested's and auto-ground lands it identically; `collapsed` is genuinely smaller and will ground lower, which is honest. One thing to expect before reading the numbers: capture_config_sweep places ONE camera from the union of all four variants, and `abreast` (about 2.8 frames wide) and `strata` (about 2.8 frames tall) both enlarge that union, so the `nested` and `collapsed` tiles will sit smaller in frame than a single-value capture would show. The silhouettes are different enough that this dilutes the bite rather than inventing one, but a low `collapsed` number should be crop-rechecked, not believed.

folding_past.description: Animated accordion fold representing time/the past collapsing into the present.
folding_past.name: Folding Past
folding_past.qfep_connection: An accordion collapsing — time made geometric, the past pleating into the present. The one primitive here that is a *metaphor* on purpose: folding as memory, the chapter admitting that even its cleanest shapes carry meaning they didn't ask for.

geometric_crystal.description: A crystal that contains spatial algorithms
geometric_crystal.name: Geometric Crystal
geometric_crystal.registry_note: RETIRED 2026-07-29 (build-or-retire triage): Registered scene is an empty stub; the crystals directory holds nothing else.

glass_planes_2_5d.description: 2.5D: Glass planes + noise. Discrete layers framing continuous field. Volumetric look, flat render cost.
glass_planes_2_5d.name: glass_planes_2_5d
glass_planes_2_5d.qfep_connection: Ten flat panes pretending to be fog: depth here is a property of the sampling, not the space, and plane_count is the dial that sets how many discrete slices the eye needs before it capitulates and reports volume. Shannon's theorem restaged in transparency.

glass_planes_empty.description: 2.5D: Array of transparent glass planes. Pure repetition â€” depth from layered transparency. No noise.
glass_planes_empty.name: glass_planes_empty
glass_planes_empty.qfep_connection: The same stack with the noise switched off — nothing between the panes but repetition, and still ten transparencies compound into depth. The control condition of 2.5D: proof the illusion needed only the array, never the content.

grab_aalto_vase.description: Grabbable Aalto vase. Procedural organic form with glass material.
grab_aalto_vase.name: grab_aalto_vase
grab_aalto_vase.qfep_connection: The Savoy silhouette regenerated from a five-number harmonics array and handed over as a pickable — you carry modernism's signature as Fourier coefficients. What Aalto sold as organic intuition, SurfaceTool restates as four cosines and a twist.

grab_alessi_tree.description: Grabbable Alessi tree. Red and white striped ceramic-style holiday decoration.
grab_alessi_tree.name: grab_alessi_tree
grab_alessi_tree.qfep_connection: Five zigzag tiers and twelve vertex-painted stripes are enough to summon December — and the summoning holds only while color_a stays white and color_b stays red. Tradition operationalized: a small parameter vector everyone tacitly agrees not to move.

grab_cube_show.name: grab_cube_show
grab_cube_show.qfep_connection: The grid's own atom mounted on a pickable chassis for exhibition — the hexahedron you see is the same Cube class the world is built from, but what your hand actually closes on is a 0.1-meter sphere collider. Display always swaps the body for a handle.

grab_dodecahedron.description: Grabbable dodecahedron. 12 pentagonal faces, 20 vertices, 30 edges.
grab_dodecahedron.name: grab_dodecahedron
grab_dodecahedron.qfep_connection: Twenty vertices placed by the golden ratio, wrapped in the grid shader so the pentagon edges glow, then handed to XRToolsPickable — a Platonic solid productively demoted to a thing the hand can turn. φ stops being a constant and becomes a weight.

grab_icosahedron.description: Grabbable icosahedron. 20 triangular faces, 12 vertices, 30 edges.
grab_icosahedron.name: grab_icosahedron
grab_icosahedron.qfep_connection: Its numbers are the dodecahedron's read backwards — twenty faces where the other has twenty vertices, twelve vertices where the other has twelve faces — and holding one in each hand is the only proof of duality that requires no algebra.

grab_line.description: Adjustable length grabbable line with trigger+joystick length control and optional length display.
grab_line.name: grab_line
grab_line.qfep_connection: One hand holds the line, the other holds its length — the tip is a second pickable, and the live label converts your stretch into meters as you feel it. Not an object but an interval: distance made grippable at both of its ends.

grab_line_drawer.description: Grabbable line that draws fading trails from the tip when trigger is held.
grab_line_drawer.name: grab_line_drawer
grab_line_drawer.qfep_connection: The endpoint refuses to forget: every move past min_draw_distance appends to a 300-sample memory that fades from the tail. Drawing exposed as retention policy — the mark is not what you make but what the buffer agrees to keep.

grab_line_music.description: Grabbable line that produces music based on movement speed and length, with selectable waveforms.
grab_line_music.name: grab_line_music
grab_line_music.qfep_connection: Length maps to pitch, hand velocity to loudness, and nothing ever quantizes the glissando — the line sings the whole continuum between its frequencies, no scale imposed. A measurement made audible before it is made discrete: E_flux with a speaker.

grab_line_pusher.name: grab_line_pusher

grab_long_stick.name: grab_long_stick
grab_long_stick.qfep_connection: F_force: the probe — a graspable stick trailing a long cloth ribbon. It is how the hand asks a soft world questions: poke, drag, sweep, and the ribbon writes the answer in folds. The instrument of contact in the softbodies rooms; force made holdable.

dna.default: dual=off - off adds no strut, leaves the mesh on the render layer it shipped on and never touches the collision shape, so all 11 placements take exactly the pre-promotion code path. apply_grid_config is new here and returns before rebuilding unless the value actually changed

axis_notes.dual: which side of the octahedron-cube duality is actually drawn. around is the circumscribing cube of half-side R, whose six face centres ARE the six vertices; inside is the inscribed cube of half-side R/3, whose eight corners ARE the eight face centres; both nests them and turns duality from a pair into a ladder. WHERE THIS DIVERGES FROM THE SIBLING: snap_octahedron_puzzle's octahedron is already a cage, so its inscribed cube is simply visible. This one is an opaque solid and an R/3 cube would be sealed inside it - the occlusion trap - so on inside and both the faces are withdrawn (layers = 0, which keeps the mesh in the capture AABB so framing does not jump) and the octahedron is drawn as its twelve edges. Which of the pair is solid and which is frame is the claim, not a second axis

grab_octahedron.description: octahedron — 6 vertices, 12 edges, 8 triangular faces: dual of the cube, Platonic solid
grab_octahedron.name: grab_octahedron
grab_octahedron.qfep_connection: Six vertices, eight faces — the cube's dual, the solid you get by putting a point on each of the cube's faces. Grabbable proof that the Platonic solids come in pairs that trade places, symmetry hiding inside symmetry.

grab_rainbow_stick.name: grab_rainbow_stick
grab_rainbow_stick.qfep_connection: the rainbow made holdable — a spectrum along a stick; the gradient as a hand tool.

grab_sphere_point.name: grab_sphere_point

grab_sphere_point_color_with_text.name: grab_sphere_point_color_with_text

grab_sphere_point_snap.name: grab_sphere_point_snap

grab_sphere_point_with_color.description: Pickable point sphere that applies emission-tinted colors via the point_color helper.
grab_sphere_point_with_color.name: grab_sphere_point_with_color_text
grab_sphere_point_with_color.qfep_connection: A point's geometry says nothing, so here its entire identity is a material — point_color rewrites albedo and emission in one call, deciding from outside what the sphere is. Identity as override; literally, material_override.

grab_sphere_point_with_text.description: Pickable point sphere preset with a floating Label3D that shows its coordinates.
grab_sphere_point_with_text.name: grab_sphere_point_with_text
grab_sphere_point_with_text.qfep_connection: Carry it and it confesses its coordinates every tenth of a second, the Label3D always one timer-tick behind the hand that moves it. Position rendered as speech — a point narrating its own address to whoever holds it.

grab_tetrahedron.name: grab_tetrahedron
grab_tetrahedron.qfep_connection: Four vertices are the cheapest way to enclose space, and the code treats them as exactly that — the same point array is both mesh and convex collision hull. What the hand grips is the claim itself: no hidden interior, geometry all the way down.

grab_trihedron.name: grab_trihedron

grab_trihedron.qfep_connection: The wedge as 3D primitive — 4 vertices, three triangular faces on a quad base. The catalyst bracelet's walkable prism in its pure geometric form: the smallest solid that can also be a ramp, where primitive meets architecture.

primitive_pillar.name: Primitive Pillar (stacked column)
primitive_pillar.description: A column built by stacking primitives course by course - boxes, drums, wedges or balls - to a height the room is told it can hold. columns x rows repeats the stack into a field, so one token is a single shaft in a corridor and a grove of them filling a room.

parameters.height_m: Pillar height in metres from the floor, clamped by clearance (default 4.20)
parameters.clearance: The room's clear height in metres (default 4.40). The museum ceiling soffit is 4.64 m over a 4.5 m wall, so 4.40 leaves a shadow gap; raise it only in an open_roof hall.
parameters.columns: Stacks across X (default 1). 1 is a corridor pillar, 3+ is a room.
parameters.footprint: The field written as 3x5 - an alias that sets columns and rows in one segment
parameters.spacing_x: Metres between stack centres across X (default 2.0)
parameters.spacing_z: Metres between stack centres along Z (default 2.0)
parameters.stock: The primitive vocabulary: box | drum | wedge | ball | mixed
parameters.wash: The colour treatment: mono | courses | gradient | spectrum
parameters.bond: How one course meets the next: stacked | staggered | gyre | taper
parameters.girth: Course width in metres (default 0.80, matching commons/primitives/pillar)
parameters.course_m: Nominal course height (default 0.55); the real height divides height_m into a whole number of courses so the stack reaches the top exactly
parameters.accent_color: r,g,b or #rrggbb - the far end of the courses and gradient washes
parameters.footer: The 0.4 m footer the pillar family stands on (bool, default true)
parameters.solid: One box collider per stack, so it is a wall and not a hologram (bool, default true)
parameters.rng_seed: Seeds every draw (stock=mixed). Same seed, same pillar, forever. (default 7)

primitive_pillar.footprint_note: footprint below describes the DEFAULT 1x1 register only. A field register needs (columns-1)*spacing_x + girth by (rows-1)*spacing_z + girth metres, which no capped footprint_cells can express - the fault pillarcolorcollection ships with, where a 9 x 15 m body declares 9 cells and the negotiator plans other bodies inside it.

dna.default: stock=box + wash=mono + bond=stacked is the lineage of commons/primitives/pillar/pillar.tscn: a plain square shaft in one stone colour on a 0.4 m footer. 0 placements exist, so no map changes.
dna.note: DERIVED from the @export_enum lines by tools/apply_dna_block.py, never transcribed. bond (stacked|staggered|gyre|taper) is exported and reachable from a map token but deliberately NOT declared as an axis: two declared axes already cross to 20 tiles, and a bite headline is a peak, so a third would hide a dead one. stock and wash are the two the pillar argues: what a column is made of, and whether colour is a property of the whole shaft or of each course. Both are visible in a single still, which a rate or a lag would not be - bond=gyre's turn is, which is why it stays a knob rather than becoming a motion axis. HEIGHT IS THE CRITICAL PARAMETER AND IT IS CLAMPED, not warned about: height_m is clamped to clearance (default 4.40) because the museum builds nothing above the 4.90 m ceiling slab and its soffit is at 4.64, so an unclamped 10 m pillar is a pillar through the ceiling. A large scale cannot arrive from a map token either: #scale: is clamped to 5.0 and token:0:0:10 parses as a three-axis rotation, so size lives in these exports.

predicted_degeneracy.pair: mono against courses, in the wash reading
predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic:
REGISTERED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, and by enumerating all 190 pairs of the 5x4 grid rather than reasoning along one axis. THE BUILD BEING PREDICTED is the bench default: columns=1, rows=1, bond=stacked, footer=true, height_m 4.20 clamped by clearance 4.40, girth 0.80, course_m 0.55. So body = 4.20 - 0.40 = 3.80 m, n = round(3.80/0.55) = 7 courses of uh = 0.5429 m, and ONE COURSE IS 1/7 = 14.3% OF THE INK - already three times the critic's hottest-5% window, which is what makes the statistic a peak delta rather than a mean.

THE TONE TERM. base (0.72,0.68,0.58), accent (0.86,0.28,0.18). mono paints all 7 courses base; courses paints the odd three at base.lerp(accent,0.65) = (0.809,0.420,0.313), a per-channel |delta| of (0.089,0.260,0.267), mean 0.2037. Three courses = 42.9% of the ink overfills the window, so focus = 0.2037 * 0.77 (the lighting-and-tonemap compression the substance_room replica measured) = 15.68%. Registered at 15.7.

WHY IT IS THE FLOOR. Every other wash pair reaches a larger peak because it reaches full base-to-accent or a hue flip: mono/spectrum 22.5, mono/gradient and courses/gradient 24.1 (the top course is pure accent against pure base), courses/spectrum 33.8, gradient/spectrum 34.2. And every stock pair flips silhouette against the corner background, which at a conservative 0.27 albedo contrast is 20.8% wherever the flipped area clears the 5% window - which it always does: the projected silhouette XOR is 24.8% of the subject for the closest stock pair (drum against ball, the ellipses inscribed in the drum's rectangle: 0.760 of 3.067 screen m2 at yaw 0.62 / pitch -0.26, where a circular plan of diameter g projects to width exactly g because the screen basis vector (0.8139, 0.5810) is unit), and 28.0 / 35.7 / 38.0 / 39.1 / 45.9 / 50.0 / 79.0 / 79.3% for the rest.

So the quietest pair in the whole sheet is a WASH pair, at every one of the five stocks, at the same 15.68 - which is itself a check: if the five mono-against-courses numbers are not equal to within render noise, the stocks are not sharing a silhouette and something is moving that should not.

THE TWO WAYS THIS CAN BE WRONG. (a) BELOW 15.7: the standing rule says stop and investigate, and the first suspects are the ones that have cost a pass each - check_dna_declarations first, then <out>/_rejects.json (a String enum handed an int is refused in SILENCE), then whether _read_metadata_overrides actually reassigned the property. Every prediction in this corpus that named a pair and a number has UNDER-read by 1.5x to 6.7x, because a flat-shaded proxy models no shadow, no AO and no antialiasing; a result under its own floor has meant a broken artifact, not a subtle one. (b) FAR ABOVE, say past 45: the courses wash is landing somewhere other than alternate courses - most likely i%2 running over the field index instead of the course index, which would recolour whole stacks and read as a much bigger change than the design makes.

grid_lines.description: grid = {x=i*step, z=j*step : i,j ∈ ℤ} — the XZ plane made legible as a lattice of lines
grid_lines.name: grid_lines
grid_lines.qfep_connection: The lattice claims to be reference, then quietly becomes a stage: saved player traces land on its intersections as scaled, rotating meshes, replaying movement as spatial memory. A coordinate system that ends up exhibiting the bodies that used it.

halocube.description: Hollow cube frame with four mitered walls
halocube.name: Halo Cube
halocube.qfep_connection: A cube stripped to four walls with corners mitred at 45° like picture framing, then rotated so the missing faces point sideways: enclosure along one axis, invitation along the other. A frame doesn't contain — it nominates a direction as the view.

dna.default: cordon=cones is a no-op. _build_scene still lays the ground with the hole, then places three traffic cones (same TAU/3 spacing, same PI/6 offset, same cone_distance, same rotation.y = angle + PI, same trafficcone.tscn), then builds the four ground collision boxes, in that order; the only change is that the cone call now sits behind `match cordon:` with cones as the first case and the export default. All 10 placements (10 direct interactable tokens in 10 maps by direct count, none of which passes a config key, plus one curation_station bay that names it in an artifacts list) are unchanged. apply_grid_config is NEW and reads exactly one key: it returns before touching anything unless `cordon` is present AND names a different value than the one already built - which matters because curation_station places this artifact in an Ontological-distance bay and calls apply_grid_config with framing keys this object has never heard of.
dna.was: four exported floats - ground size, hole radius, ground colour, cone distance - no apply_grid_config at all, so every config key a map could send was silently discarded, and the warning was welded to the pit: three cones or three cones.
dna.note: The hole is the artifact; the cones are the SPEECH ACT about the hole, and they were fused to it. A hazard is not what is missing but what the surrounding matter has been made to announce, and the object could make only one announcement. cones is the shipped site: portable, provisional, stackable, a warning that expects to be taken away again. tape draws the perimeter and stops nobody - a line, not an obstacle, the rest left to your judgement. barrier is the warning become a wall: it no longer addresses your judgement, it removes the choice, and safe and permitted stop being separate things. none is the control case - the danger entirely real and saying nothing, the floor reading as floor until you are in it, which is what proves the other four were speech rather than geometry. covered is the most common answer on a real site and the most double-edged: the pit is not declared but sealed, the ground reads whole, and the absence has been made invisible rather than safe. Marking and concealing turn out to be the same gesture taken one step further.
dna.kin: `warning` (force_vortex, path_cube, path_wedge and eight more: none|stain|cage|beacon|shroud) asks this exact question and was declined, because the list cannot transfer character for character: the shipped default here is a specific piece of real-world equipment, cones, which is not in that list, and the default has to reproduce the pre-change behaviour. Taking the word with a different list would put two incompatible value sets behind one name, which is the state `presence` got into. `guard` (library_rack, exhibit_vitrine, exhibit_furniture: none|label|fixture|hood|cordon) holds cordon as one of its VALUES, a vitrine's barrier among four other things a display can do; here the cordon is the whole speech act rather than one option inside it, so it is the axis name. Nearest in spirit is you_are_here's `deixis`, promoted the same day - both artifacts are about what a sign claims - and the values deliberately do not rhyme, because one addresses a body and the other marks a pit.
dna.harness_note: The subject is a 4 m ground plane and the cordon occupies the middle metre of it, so a whole-AABB fit will dilute the difference; if the tiles read faint, crop to the middle before calling the axis inert - none and cones differ by three cones on an otherwise identical 4 m square. covered is the one value that also changes the ground reading (the pit disappears) and is therefore the strongest tile; barrier is the next. tape and barrier carry no collision by design - they are declarations, and the artifact has always been an environment piece you can walk through the props of - while covered DOES add a collision plate, because a picture of sealed ground that you fall through would be lying in one sense and telling the truth in the other.

hole_with_cones.description: Ground plane with circular hole and 3 traffic cones around it. Construction site warning setup.

hollowrock.description: Hollow rock using torus with varied openings
hollowrock.name: Hollow Rock
