horizon_plumb_lines.name: horizon_plumb_lines
horizon_plumb_lines.qfep_connection: Two verticals hung 0.4 m apart do nothing but agree on up, each still reporting its own length label. Parallelism staged as a felt fact: the eye keeps checking that the gap never closes, performing the fifth postulate as a posture.

icosahedron.description: Procedural icosahedron primitive for sphere approximations.
icosahedron.name: icosahedron
icosahedron.qfep_connection: Three orthogonal golden rectangles pinned at their corners — the roundest the Platonic family ever gets, and it gets there by leaning on an irrational number it can never fully spend.

interactive_point_origin_force.description: Force-catalyst variant of interactive_point_origin. Starts as a plain point; on pickup a vertex shader morphs the surface into a pulsing 'force field' shell. While held with the morph engaged, nearby RigidBody3D objects feel an inverse-square pull toward the artifact. With both hands closed (the OrbGestureDetector two-hand gesture), the artifact spits a luminous projectile ball forward.
interactive_point_origin_force.name: 1.0.2 Interactive Point — Force Catalyst

parameters.attraction_radius: Sphere radius (m) within which RigidBody3D bodies feel the pull. Default 1.5.
parameters.attraction_strength: Pull-force coefficient k in F = k / d². Default 8.0.
parameters.ball_speed: Initial velocity (m/s) of two-hand projectile balls. Default 6.0.

parameters.morph_speed: How fast morph_t lerps from 0 → 1 on pickup. Default 1.4 (≈0.7s).

interactive_point_origin_force.qfep_connection: F_force: the origin point that becomes a force field in the hand — picked up, its surface morphs to a pulsing shell that pushes nearby bodies. The coordinate origin revealed as an actor, not an address.

dna.default: mark=bead - the lineage exactly: the 30 mm sphere point_mesh.gd writes into the host MeshInstance3D before this script's _ready runs, layers left at 1, and no Mark node allocated at all (_build_mark returns before it builds anything). Every placement is a bare token - Annotation_Demo and FoldStudio_Preview's @signature reference it directly, Corridor_Point_One and Curation_Bay_primitives_3 list it inside a curation_station - and apply_grid_config returns unless a token names `mark` AND the word differs from the one already held, so no shipped placement is ever torn down.
dna.was: twelve exports and not one about the point. Four haptic durations, two sound and glow settings, a line colour and width, an origin vector: dials on FEEDBACK and HANDLING, on the project's first primitive, whose whole subject is what a coordinate is. No apply_grid_config either, so no map token could reach anything.
dna.note: A position has no extension, and what stands in the room is a 60 mm ball with a light in it. The bead is a lie about size told so smoothly that the lesson is built on it. Each value re-tells it differently and drops something: crosshair drops the volume (three bars along X, Y, Z and nothing at the crossing - the position is the intersection of its coordinates, and what you see is a reach); cage drops the point itself (twelve edges of the cell and nothing inside, which is what a voxel world actually stores - an address with walls); halo drops the claim that the size is the thing's (a thin ring around a 4 mm speck: the mark declares itself a mark). All three are sized to the bead they replace, so this is a claim about form, not a size dial.
dna.declined: the LINE TO ORIGIN, which is this artifact's own named critical parameter, and `readout`, the family word xyz_slider_plate and line share for exactly this question. Both are invisible to the evidence. The line exists only while held and the label is visible=false until a hand closes on it, and the still is of an object nobody is holding. Worse for the line: the sweep bench parents the artifact straight under the viewport, so it stands ON the origin, `distance < 0.001` returns early, and four values of a tether axis would render the identical picture of no line - the 0.00%-to-the-byte failure with four values instead of two.
dna.kin: grab_sphere_F/E/lambda/phi carry `grasp` (atom, socket, chorus, hollow, swarm) on a 24 mm sphere in this same folder, and that is the neighbouring question - what your hand closes on. Deliberately NOT reused: those spheres stand for terms of a formula, things with no referent at all, and `chorus` puts the other three terms on a rail. A coordinate has a perfectly good referent, a place, so the question here is how a place is marked, not what a term is.
dna.reach_note: reachable from the two direct grid placements only. curation_station instantiates its children without forwarding a config token (the same wrapper gap reported on the grasp family), so the two listed inside a bay stay bead whatever a map says.
dna.framing_note: framing 0.3 because the subject is 6-12 cm and the capture's radius floor (0.2 m) frames it at about 8% of the frame - the documented dilution that reads as a faint axis. The Mark node hangs under the existing MeshInstance3D, not under the root, so the root's direct-children set that GridInteractablesComponent walks to ground the artifact is unchanged.

interactive_point_origin.description: Pickable point that displays its position and draws a thin line to origin (0,0,0) when held.
interactive_point_origin.name: 1.0.1 Interactive Point with Origin Line
interactive_point_origin.qfep_connection: Every position is a debt to (0,0,0): lift the point and a thin line names its creditor, while each pickup cycles the coordinate through four notations — the number never changes, only its costume.

interactivetriangle.description: Standing triangle panel split into pink and black faces with grab spheres and multiple shape resets.
interactivetriangle.name: 1.2: A triangle
interactivetriangle.qfep_connection: The triangle as a panel you argue with — pink and black faces, grab spheres, presets to snap between shapes. The subject made operable: not a triangle shown but a triangle *handled*, its three-ness confirmed by your own hands moving the corners.

knowledge_prism.description: Prism that refracts complex concepts into understandable forms
knowledge_prism.name: Knowledge Prism
knowledge_prism.qfep_connection: The prism adds nothing to the light — every colour leaving it was already in the beam that entered, and the wedge only stops them travelling together. Separation is not creation: a thing that looks singular is usually just a thing nobody has bent yet.

kochsnowflake.name: kochsnowflake
kochsnowflake.qfep_connection: Perimeter grows by four-thirds per recursion while the triangle stays put, and the ImmediateMesh of bare line pairs renders that honestly: the infinite coastline is always shown at some finite depth d. The parameter is the confession — infinity is a budget of segments the recursion spends.

laser_measure.description: Handheld laser distance measurement tool with LCD display
laser_measure.name: laser_measure
laser_measure.qfep_connection: The handheld ruler with an LCD conscience: point, and the world answers in meters. Measurement as a portable act — the abstraction of the line turned into a tool you carry, distance no longer a property of two points but a question you can ask anywhere.

lefttriangle.description: Complementary right-triangle prism leaning left, rendered with pink grid shading and configurable size.
lefttriangle.name: lefttriangle
lefttriangle.qfep_connection: The mirror-twin of the right-leaning wedge, pink and 10 cm thin — chirality as content. No rotation in the plane turns leaning-left into leaning-right; the slab holds a difference only reflection can erase, and reflection is the move the grid never makes on its own.

level_entrance.description: Entrance tile with door frame and label text
level_entrance.name: Level Entrance
level_entrance.qfep_connection: A doorway whose entire mechanism is a name: cross the frame and the Area3D emits its label text as a signal. Passage and naming fused — the threshold doesn't move you anywhere, it announces what you consented to enter.

light_sphere.name: light_sphere
light_sphere.qfep_connection: A forty-meter mirrored sphere occupied from the inside, reflection probe and omni light included: not an object in the room but the lighting condition the rest of the room is seen under.

lightrod.description: Glowing vertical blue light rods. Use lightrod:90:0:1#config:4:1 for 4 rods with 1m spacing.
lightrod.name: Light Rod
lightrod.qfep_connection: Glowing verticals at set spacing — the line standing up and repeating. Rhythm from the simplest rule: same element, even interval. The primitive learning that pattern is just a primitive plus a beat.

line.description: Interactive measuring line linking two grab spheres and rendering a cylinder with live distance text.
line.name: 1.1 A Line
line.qfep_connection: Two points consent to a relationship and a line is born, its length live between them. The primitive after the point, and the first thing in the project with an *inside* — a here-to-there. Distance made grabbable: measurement as the second thing that exists.

line_collection.description: Bundle of line modules offset in space for demonstrations of multiple edges.
line_collection.name: line_collection
line_collection.qfep_connection: Three copies of the same labelled segment stacked at heights 0, 0.15, 0.27 — offsets just irregular enough that the eye asks whether the stack is a pattern or an accident. Multiplicity begins the moment one becomes three without a rule.

line_demo.description: snap_connection(pointA, pointB) → line — demonstrate the SnapConnectionManager wiring
line_demo.name: line_demo
line_demo.qfep_connection: The line exists only after two snap points pass the manager's category validation — proximity alone earns no connection here. And the instant a link forms, the instruction display hides itself: explanation staged as scaffolding that a working relation makes redundant, returning only when the connection breaks.

lshape.description: Upside down L shape primitive. DNA: corner selects HOW THE TWO ARMS MEET — joint (the arms share the corner cell and the notch is explicit geometry), butt (the column runs full height and the arm lands on its side), mitre (a 45 degree seam, neither member continuous), gap (the arms never touch and the L exists only in the eye). Use #corner:mitre.

dna.default: corner=joint - the original vertex/face lists are still the joint branch, called verbatim, so all 12 existing placements render the identical mesh
dna.was: zero exports: one fixed cyan L whose own @identity named 'the corner joint geometry' as its critical parameter while offering no way to turn it
dna.note: The artifact's truth statement is that a non-convex shape cannot be a single box. corner=gap is the value that argues back — the arms stop touching and the L survives anyway, as an adjacency claim the geometry refuses to make.

lshape.name: L Shape
lshape.qfep_connection: An upside-down L, two beams meeting at a corner joint — the first primitive that is *assembled* rather than born, a shape made of shapes. Where the alphabet starts spelling.

mengersponge.description: Menger sponge fractal with configurable depth
mengersponge.name: Menger Sponge
mengersponge.qfep_connection: Twenty of twenty-seven cubes survive each pass; the code writes the sponge as a removal policy, never as a shape. What renders is the residue of a subtraction applied to its own output — volume draining toward zero, surface toward infinity, F_order as pure deletion.

menu.description: Stacked slanted-cube VR menu with animated hover, keyboard navigation, and theme switching.
menu.name: menu
menu.qfep_connection: PLAY, OPTIONS, ABOUT, QUIT as slanted cubes in a vertical stack — the interface refuses to be a flat overlay and takes a body in the room instead. Even quitting gets mass, a crimson, and a position you must physically face.

modernchair.description: Modern chair with configurable seat, legs and backrest
modernchair.name: Modern Chair
modernchair.qfep_connection: Fifty-odd vertices quoted verbatim from a Blender export, then stretched by seat, leg, and back parameters — furniture as frozen citation wearing adjustable proportions. The exports promise any chair; the vertex list remembers only the one that was modelled.

modernpolysolid.description: Twisted multi-level polysolid sculpture with pride-inspired materials.
modernpolysolid.name: modernpolysolid
modernpolysolid.qfep_connection: Octagon to hexagon to square, each level rotated against the one below — a column that trades its symmetry group down floor by floor while staying one continuous body. Twist is the argument: identity persists precisely by not repeating itself.

noisetorus_ex_1.description: Example torus mesh using the noise planet shader to showcase parameter tweaks.
noisetorus_ex_1.name: noisetorus_ex_1
noisetorus_ex_1.qfep_connection: A stock TorusMesh handed to the noise-planet shader with every dial frozen — noise_scale 0.955, height 0.365, hue drifting at 0.05. An example promoted to artifact: the shader's parameter space is the real object, and this is one pinned point in it, still slowly cycling color to prove the field is alive.

octahedron.description: Procedural octahedron primitive useful as a diamond core.
octahedron.name: octahedron
octahedron.qfep_connection: Six vertices are the coordinate axes made solid — hold it and you hold plus and minus x, y, z — while the cube waits inside its face centers for the dual swap.

one_meter_line.name: one_meter_line
one_meter_line.qfep_connection: Two endpoints set exactly a metre apart and nothing more: the SI unit as an inhabitable prop. In a headset rendered 1:1 it is the rare object whose size is a claim about your body rather than about itself — the invariant everything else in the room is silently measured against.

origin.description: (0, 0, 0) — the reference from which all coordinates are measured
origin.name: Point Zero
origin.qfep_connection: (0,0,0) — the reference from which all coordinates are measured, and the chapter's true first artifact. Everything in this project has an address because this point agreed to be zero. A decision disguised as a fact: someone had to choose where nothing begins.

oscillation_cube.description: A cube that demonstrates smooth oscillating motion along multiple axes
oscillation_cube.name: Oscillation Cube
oscillation_cube.qfep_connection: Three periodic motions — spin, sine bob, scale pulse — each with its own on/off switch, so the compound dance can be decomposed live into its factors. Superposition taught by subtraction: silence two and discover what the third was doing all along.

parallel_line_puzzle.description: Interactive puzzle: drag line endpoints to align two lines to be parallel.
parallel_line_puzzle.name: Parallel Line Puzzle
parallel_line_puzzle.qfep_connection: Drag two lines until they will never meet. The puzzle makes 'parallel' a thing your hands discover rather than a word you're told — and quietly seeds the crisis chapter, where the promise these lines keep turns out to have been a choice all along.

dna.default: pair_pose=upright, start_state=parallel - both generators collapse to the shipped literal coordinates at 0 degrees tilt, so the 8 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: four target vertices and two starting segments written as literal arrays: the finished pair could only ever be two vertical posts, and the two lines were handed over already parallel to each other, so the learner transported a parallelism instead of making one
dna.note: declared by hand 2026-07-29 - the artifact exposed no @export of its own and the sweep refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS; the pose of the pair and the state it is handed over in were the constants carrying the argument

parallel_lines.description: Three line modules arranged in parallel to visualize equidistant lines.
parallel_lines.name: parallel_lines
parallel_lines.qfep_connection: f_order: three lines holding their distance forever — Euclid's fifth postulate standing in the room as furniture, so ordinary that its overthrow next door lands as vertigo.

parametric_surface.name: Parametric Surface
parametric_surface.qfep_connection: Two variables in, one twisted shell out: the whole form hangs on cos(v)(1+cos u)sin(v/8), and moving v_max decides how much of the shape is permitted to exist.

dna.default: vanishing_points=one, reach=touch - every endpoint forced to Vector3.ZERO at full travel, wearing the single shipped colour (1.0, 0.3, 0.5), which is literally the code that has always run, so all 10 existing placements are pixel-identical
dna.was: the shared origin is this artifact's own declared critical_parameter and it was a literal Vector3.ZERO, with the four frame corners, the 0.008 thickness and the pink all inlined in setup_perspective_lines() and no apply_grid_config() at all. The piece could state one-point perspective and nothing else - it could not say that a vanishing point belongs to a family of parallels rather than to the world.
dna.note: vanishing_points is not a count of lines - the scene still has exactly four, and at every value they still run from the same rectangular frame. What changes is how many origins those four are forced to share, which is the whole claim. In two- and three-point modes the lines are tinted by family so you can see which parallels answer to which point; in one-point mode all four keep the shipped colour, so the default is untouched. reach answers the identity line that calls the vanishing point 'a limit, not a place' - the shipped drawing contradicted it by letting the cylinders arrive and stop.

perspective_lines.description: all lines → (0,0,0) — convergence to a single vanishing point as perspective law
perspective_lines.name: perspective_lines
perspective_lines.qfep_connection: All lines running to one point — the vanishing point, perspective's single law. The Renaissance's most consequential primitive: the discovery that depth on a flat surface is just convergence, that space can be faked by a ruler aimed at infinity. The line taught to lie about distance, and the whole illusion of the third dimension riding on that one honest trick.

pickup_cube_combo.description: A pickup cube that moves, rotates, and scales simultaneously.
pickup_cube_combo.name: Combo Pickup Cube
pickup_cube_combo.qfep_connection: Translation, rotation, and scale run simultaneously on the visual child while the wrapper zeroes its own motion and strips the inner collision so your body can enter it. Composition is the lesson — S as a product of maps — and the score registers the instant you step inside the product.

pickup_cube_rotating.description: Pickup cube that rotates continuously — wraps pick_up_cube.gd and disables internal collision so the player can walk into the pickup area freely.
pickup_cube_rotating.name: Rotating Pickup Cube
pickup_cube_rotating.qfep_connection: oscillation: a pickup cube in rotation — periodic motion in the hand; frequency you can grip.

pickup_cube_scaling.description: A pickup cube that pulsates in size.
pickup_cube_scaling.name: Scaling Pickup Cube
pickup_cube_scaling.qfep_connection: The cube breathes: scale oscillates while position and rotation stay pinned, isolating one column of the transform matrix as rhythm. The detection box never changes size while the visuals pulse — what you collect is the invariant, not the throb.

pickup_cube_static.description: A static pickup cube that can be collected.
pickup_cube_static.name: Static Pickup Cube
pickup_cube_static.qfep_connection: a pickup cube, still — the baseline state; hold it to feel zero oscillation.

pickup_cube_transforming.description: A pickup cube that moves up and down.
pickup_cube_transforming.name: Transforming Pickup Cube
pickup_cube_transforming.qfep_connection: a pickup cube mid-transformation — states cycling; change as the held constant.

plane.description: Grid-shaded plane mesh (0.8m square) used for flat surface demonstrations.
plane.name: plane
plane.qfep_connection: Ten-by-ten segments drawn on a surface that would be featureless without them — the tessellation exists so flatness can be perceived at all. Zero curvature leaves no evidence of its own; the lattice is the testimony.

platonic_demo.name: platonic_demo
platonic_demo.qfep_connection: A finite family passed hand to hand: the five closed solids share a shelf with a grab-trihedron that geometry refuses to close, and the snap code treats the legitimate and the impossible exactly alike.

platonic_grabbables.description: Compact table of all 5 platonic solids, 3 grabbable copies each. Tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, icosahedron.
platonic_grabbables.name: platonic_grabbables
platonic_grabbables.qfep_connection: All five Platonic solids on one table, three grabbable copies each — the complete set of perfectly regular volumes, which antiquity thought were the elements themselves. Pick them up and hold the fact Plato held: there are exactly five, and no more are possible, a scarcity built into space.

player_trace.capacity: SEE your own motion become a drawable path through time.
player_trace.description: A recorder that turns the player's motion into a visible line in space. Every step writes another point, so translation through the room becomes geometry rather than a forgotten action. The artifact makes path and trajectory tangible, especially when compared against grids and axis-constrained motion. It turns movement into a time-indexed drawing.
interactions: walk through space to extend the trace
change trail_length to keep more or less motion history
compare your recorded path against grid or axis demonstrations
use the line as a visible record of translation over time
player_trace.name: player_trace
player_trace.qfep_connection: Transformation is recorded here as a trajectory through S over time. The body changes position continuously, while the trace preserves that history as form.

dna.default: symmetry=c4 - all four arms reach arm_length exactly as the single hard-coded value did, giving the identical mesh and identical two-box collision, so all 9 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: no exports: one arm_length reaching in all four directions, so the C4 symmetry the artifact is about was welded shut and could not be broken to be seen

plus.description: Plus/cross shape (+) with 4 arms at 90 degree angles. Classic health pickup shape.
plus.name: Plus
plus.qfep_connection: Four arms at right angles — the cross, and every player's memory of a health pickup. Symmetry at its most legible: rotate it a quarter turn and nothing changes, the primitive that teaches invariance before the symmetry chapter names it.

plus_line_puzzle.description: Interactive puzzle: drag line endpoints to form a + (plus) with perpendicular lines.
plus_line_puzzle.name: Plus Line Puzzle

dna.default: proof=relation, stock=stacked - the pre-promotion behaviour exactly (four marks required, perpendicular + crossing at centres, two parallel lines waiting below), so all 8 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: no exports of its own: the figure, the starting layout and the success condition were all hard-coded in _init(), so the sweep found no turnable knob

plus_line_puzzle.qfep_connection: Drag the endpoints until two lines cross at right angles — a plus, a cross, the first perpendicular. The puzzle where the hand discovers orthogonality: that 90 degrees is not given but *made*, a relation you can satisfy or miss, and the quiet foundation of every grid this world is built on.

plus_lines.description: Reusable plus-shaped line rig built from two line segments for crosshair highlights.
plus_lines.name: plus_lines
plus_lines.qfep_connection: Two identical segments, one rotated ninety degrees — the plus is the minimal act of orientation, making across out of two copies of along. Each arm still reports its own length label, unaware it has become a symbol.

point.description: Pickable point sphere that continuously displays its world coordinates with a floating label.
point.name: 1.0 A Point

dna.default: frame=world, attach=float - reproduces the shipped label exactly (same format string with its inherited 'local position:' caption, same global reading, same 0.1 billboard offset), so the 7 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: zero exports - a Label3D built in code, billboarded yellow above the grab sphere, printing the sphere's global position under a caption that called it local
dna.reads: frame chooses the origin a point measures itself from (and mute takes the address away entirely); attach decides whether the address turns to face the reader or belongs to the place

point.qfep_connection: A grabbable nothing that answers with three numbers: move the sphere and the label re-reports (x, y, z) every frame. Location shown as an address rather than a thing, and the whole primitives sequence grows from that admission.

point_collection.description: Grouped set of labelled pickable points for demonstrating multiple coordinate references.
point_collection.name: point_collection
point_collection.qfep_connection: Four labelled grab-spheres parked at the corners of a 0.4 m square: lift one and the configuration stops being a square. Position is a property only while nobody's hand is in the data — coordinates turn negotiable the moment they are pickable.

portal_frame.description: Portal doorway frame with three-plate lintel
portal_frame.name: Portal Frame
portal_frame.qfep_connection: Two posts and a three-plate lintel spend every triangle on the frame and none on the passage. A door is the architectural admission that the load-bearing part of a wall is its absence.

prism.description: Grid-shaded triangular prism mesh for primitive previews.
prism.name: prism

prism_block.capacity: COMPARE how a non-cubic primitive responds to rotation and scaling.
prism_block.description: A triangular prism used as reference geometry when cubes are too symmetrical to show the difference clearly. Rotating or scaling it changes which faces dominate the view, so the artifact makes orientation and aspect easier to read. It is a reminder that transformations act on more than boxes. The prism broadens the learner's sense of what can stay invariant under change.
interactions: place the prism beside cubes as a comparison shape
inspect how triangular faces reorient under rotation
use the block as a reference for scaling exercises
compare its silhouette against more symmetric primitives
prism_block.name: prism_block
prism_block.qfep_connection: Transformation changes pose and size while the prism's edge structure stays coherent. A less symmetric primitive makes preserved relations easier to notice.

dna.default: grain=solid - the shipped code path, so existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: the prism's sibling of cube_scene.grain — the same question of internal division, asked of the non-cubic solid
dna.note: declared by hand 2026-07-29 — the axis was already in the script and the registry had never been told, so the sweep could not reach it

prismblock.description: Triangular wedge primitive with grid shader and convex collision.
prismblock.name: prismblock
prismblock.qfep_connection: A rectangular base rising to an off-center ridge — the first primitive whose top differs from its bottom. The hardcoded ridge_offset of 0.15 carries the whole message: symmetry broken by a single constant, direction born from one number.

probability_sphere.description: A sphere that shows the dance of randomness
probability_sphere.name: Probability Sphere
probability_sphere.qfep_connection: Density is the argument, not the generator: the same fixed directions are re-seated along their own rays by the chosen inverse CDF, so four wholly different-looking objects are provably one sample space occupied differently. Probability here is a way of crowding a room rather than a number a machine emits — which is why it can stand in a sequence where randomness has not yet been taught.

proceduralrock.description: Procedural rock using icosphere and noise deformation
proceduralrock.name: Procedural Rock
proceduralrock.qfep_connection: An icosphere roughened by four octaves of simplex noise — the natural staged as sphere-plus-deviation. E_flux is the costume; underneath, Plato's roundest solid persists, and every regeneration re-rolls the disguise without ever touching the body.

profile_chair.description: Profile chair with integrated seat and backrest corners
profile_chair.name: Profile Chair
profile_chair.qfep_connection: Legs, seat, and back as one side-elevation extruded 8 cm thick — the draughtsman's view made solid. You cannot sit on it because it is the profile of sitting, not the affordance; the drawing convention has been given collision.

dna.default: base_sides=4, apex_stance=centred - a square base with the apex directly over its centre. base_sides=4 returns the original literal four-corner list rather than the polygon formula, and centred is the original (0, height, 0), so the geometry is bit-for-bit what it was and the 8 existing placements are unchanged.
dna.was: No exports at all - the sweep refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. base_size 0.6 and pyramid_height 0.8 were private vars, and the two constants the word 'pyramid' is really hiding were not variables at all: the base was a hard-coded four-corner literal and the apex was hard-coded to (0, h, 0). Every placement in the project showed the same right square pyramid, and the face list was a fixed six-triangle table.
dna.note: Hand promotion. base_sides makes the base polygon a variable, so 'pyramid' reads as a family (tetrahedron at 3) rather than a shape; apex_stance separates right from oblique - same base, same height, same volume by Cavalieri, but the apex has left the centre. Face generation is now a base fan plus one triangle per base edge, which reproduces the old table exactly at 4 sides.

pyramid.description: Procedural square-based pyramid primitive built via surface tool.
pyramid.name: pyramid
pyramid.qfep_connection: The square base lifts to a point and the plane becomes a volume — the first primitive with a *height*, built face by face from the surface tool. Position, then line, then face, then this: the fourth step, where flat space finally admits it was hiding a third direction.

dna.default: constraint=free - the constraint code never runs and no handle position is ever written back, which is exactly the pre-promotion behaviour, so the 11 existing placements are unchanged.
dna.was: No exports and no apply_grid_config at all - the sweep refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. Five handles, every one of them independent, in every placement. The artifact's own @identity listed 'missing symmetry-lock toggle' under needs, so the axis was already named in the file; it just was not reachable from a map.
dna.note: Hand promotion. The truth line says a pyramid is just a parameterisation; the axis adds that a parameterisation is defined by what it forbids. symmetric mirrors the moved base corner into the other three and pins the apex to the centre axis, so dragging can never leave the family of right pyramids; apex_only freezes the base and stages the truth line literally; base_only nails the apex and deforms the footprint under it.
dna.sweep_note: 0.10% — INTERACTION-DEPENDENT, not inert. `constraint` governs which degrees of freedom the grab handles offer, so it only manifests when a hand drags one. A still shows the same pyramid under every value because nothing has been dragged. Judge this axis in a map, not from a sheet.

pyramid_edit.description: Interactive pyramid demo with grab handles to reshape the base and apex.
pyramid_edit.name: pyramid_edit
pyramid_edit.qfep_connection: The pyramid with handles: reshape the base, drag the apex, watch the volume answer. Solid geometry made clay — the subject confirmed by deformation, the walker learning a shape by breaking and remaking it.

dna.default: stature=spire, apex_stance=centred - spire returns the literal 2.8 the artifact shipped with rather than a computed ratio, and centred is the original (0, height, 0), so the five vertices and the six-face table are bit-for-bit what they were and the 6 existing placements are unchanged.
dna.was: No exports at all - the sweep refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. pyramid_height 2.8, base_width 0.8 and base_length 0.8 were private vars, and the apex was hard-coded to (0, pyramid_height, 0). The @identity block already named the constant that mattered - 'critical_parameter: pyramid_height = 2.8 - taller than wide' - but it could not be turned, so every placement showed the same pink spire.
dna.note: Hand promotion. stature is not a size knob: the base never moves, only the proportion above it, which is exactly the claim in this artifact's truth line - same topology, different story. mound is half the base, even squares the profile, needle doubles the spire again. apex_stance is borrowed verbatim from the pyramid sibling promoted the same day, so the two read as one family and a leaning spire can be compared with a leaning mound. base_sides was deliberately NOT taken here: the sibling already owns that axis, and this artifact's own hidden constant is the aspect ratio.

pyramidlong.description: Procedurally models a long rectangular pyramid primitive with computed faces and materials.
pyramidlong.name: pyramidlong
pyramidlong.qfep_connection: A long rectangular pyramid, faces and materials computed on the fly — the pyramid stretched until it becomes a wedge, a roof, a prow. Proof that the primitives are a *family* of proportions, not a fixed set of nouns.

pythagorean_proof.description: Interactive right-triangle construction with draggable vertices and animated area proof squares.
pythagorean_proof.name: pythagorean_proof
pythagorean_proof.qfep_connection: Drag a vertex and the three squares re-derive their areas live — a² + b² = c² held not as formula but as a constraint you can stress with your hand. The proof survives your interference, and that survival, felt through the controller, is what theorem means.

pythagorean_triangle.name: pythagorean_triangle
pythagorean_triangle.qfep_connection: Rightness here is maintained, not given: drag a vertex within 0.4 m of orthogonality and the code pulls it onto the perpendicular line, squares blooming on each side. The right angle is a norm with a capture radius — you feel the geometry recruit you back.

pythagorean_triangle_angles.description: a² + b² = c² — the Pythagorean theorem made spatial: three squares grown from triangle sides
pythagorean_triangle_angles.name: 1.2: A pythagorean_triangle_angles

dna.default: evidence=result - a deliberate no-op. _apply_evidence() returns on its first line while evidence is result and no proof node has been built, so the shipped exhibit constructs not one extra node, runs not one extra call, and the three squares keep the visibility they were born with. The formula label trim is gated on axiom alone. All 5 existing placements draw the identical triangle, squares, arcs and arithmetic.
dna.was: four exports and every one a dial: sphere_size_multiplier, sphere_y_offset, arc_radius and a freeze flag. The exhibit grew three squares from the three sides and printed a^2 + b^2 = c^2 with the numbers filled in - it ASSERTED the theorem and left the proof off-stage. There was no apply_grid_config at all, so no map token could reach even the dials.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03, refused by the runner for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The hard-coded constant that was secretly a parameter space is not a number here, it is a choice about what gets drawn: the altitude foot, the shear and Euclid I.47 were all computable from the three vertices the artifact already tracks, and none of them were drawn. axiom hides all three squares and keeps the claim line only - the theorem stated, nothing shown. result is the shipped exhibit. trace shears the two leg squares into equal-area parallelograms leaning along the altitude, the sliding proof held still. longhand is Euclid I.47: the altitude produced through the hypotenuse square, cutting it into the rectangle of area a^2 and the rectangle of area b^2, each drawn in its own leg square's colour. The four values are a ladder from assertion to demonstration and every rung is a different picture in a still.
dna.kin: evidence is the corpus family word, reused character for character (result|trace|longhand|axiom, 19 declarations) and this artifact measures alike with them: the question is whether the working is on show or only the answer. It is the same axis lsystem_tree took in this pass, and the two are honest siblings - one shows the derivation of a string, the other the dissection of a square, both asking whether the learner is handed a result or a route to it.

pythagorean_triangle_angles.qfep_connection: a² + b² = c², grown as three real squares from a triangle's sides so the theorem stops being algebra and becomes area you can see balance. The oldest proof in the building, made spatial — measurement's first law standing in the room as furniture.

quad.description: Editable quad divided into pink and black triangles with draggable corners and square/rectangle/diamond presets.
quad.name: quad
quad.qfep_connection: Four corners, two triangles wearing one skin — the quad is the triangle's compromise with convenience, the face that tiles a wall. Split into pink and black it shows its seam honestly: every rectangle in this world is two triangles keeping a secret.

quad_line_puzzle.description: Interactive puzzle: drag 4 line endpoints to form a square.
quad_line_puzzle.name: Quad Line Puzzle

dna.default: figure=square, plane=upright - the four hard-coded corner literals verbatim, so the 7 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: no exports of its own: four Vector3 literals in _init, so the only quad you could ever be asked to close was a square standing in the air

quad_line_puzzle.qfep_connection: Drag four endpoints until they close into a square. The puzzle where lines learn to become an enclosure — the hand discovering that four right angles is a *condition*, not a given, and that a shape is a set of relationships you can satisfy or break.

quantum_dice.description: Dice that demonstrate quantum probability principles
quantum_dice.name: Quantum Dice
quantum_dice.qfep_connection: Six face weights drive six emission energies, so a loaded die and a fair one are visually distinct before any roll. The distribution stops hiding inside opaque physics and becomes light on the surface — a chart you can throw.

dna.default: face=bullseye, flag=progress - together these ARE the shipped object. bullseye is the `_:` branch of the match and runs the loop that used to be inline in _generate_rings, line for line: radius_step = max_radius / n, palette[0] outermost, a 1 mm z-offset per ring, cylinders rotated 90 degrees on X. progress returns the same eight Progress Pride colours in the same order the literal array carried. All 3 placements (ForcesArena and Forces_Drone_Game at rotations 90 and -90, VFM_08_Arena bare) pass no config key at all, and apply_grid_config returns before touching anything unless a word actually moved. Neither axis reaches the CollisionShape3D, the audio, the particles, the flash tween or the score: every arrangement is hit in exactly the same way.
dna.was: five magnitude exports (points_per_hit, breathing_speed, breathing_amount, target_radius and target_thickness - the last of which the build never read) and no apply_grid_config at all. Both of the lists that decide what this object IS were hard-coded, and the palette carried the comment `(removed outer yellow/orange/red)`: an editorial decision about which stripes it wears, left in a parenthesis.
dna.note: The identity block already claimed that 'the same geometry is two cultural objects depending on intent - flag when still, target when sighted' about a build that only ever produced one of the two. face makes the claim checkable rather than asserted: bands is the flag standing where the target stood, with no centre for the colours to converge on; spokes puts every colour the same distance from the middle so no ring is the bull and none the outer; column lays the face down into a ziggurat that faces nobody, which the truth line says a target cannot do. flag is the second hard-coded list: rainbow is the 1979 six-stripe the shipped palette is a revision of, trans is the only symmetric palette here (it has no outer), full restores what the source comment removed, and archery is the regulation FITA face - the object with the flag taken off it, which is the counterfactual the artifact needs. Ring count follows palette size, so flag changes the geometry and not only the colour. A new export, breathing_phase, defaults to -1.0 = the shipped random start phase per instance; dna.fixture pins it at 2.0 for the sweep, because otherwise the 2 percent breathing scale walks between frames and arrives in the critic numbers dressed as the axis.

queer_cylinder_target.description: A target face built from Progress Pride stripes: eight concentric emissive disks, outermost first, each a millimetre in front of the last, breathing gently on a sine. Hits anywhere flash every ring white, fire a burst of coloured cubes and score - the same surface reads as a flag when still and as a target when sighted.
queer_cylinder_target.name: queer_cylinder_target
queer_cylinder_target.qfep_connection: a target that takes the hit and keeps its difference — the cylinder the throwing room aims at; consequence's address.

quest_controller.description: Procedural Quest Touch controller model for tutorials. Use #highlight:trigger/grip/thumbstick/button_a/button_b/menu and #right:true/false
quest_controller.name: Quest Controller
quest_controller.qfep_connection: The instrument of every other interaction gets exiled into the world of objects: capsule, tracking ring, seven named parts, one of which can be told to glow cyan. Teaching the hand requires first setting its prosthesis down where it can be pointed at.

random_object_spawner.description: A spawning algorithm that randomly generates and places objects in the environment
random_object_spawner.name: Random Object Spawner

dna.fixture_note: UNPHOTOGRAPHABLE WITHOUT THIS, by construction. The first cube arrives at next_spawn_time = 1.0 s and the shutter opens at SETTLE = 1.1 s, so every variant of every axis renders the same single cube; and the duplicated grab_cube_wood is a live RigidBody3D, so on a bench with no floor it has fallen six metres by the time it is photographed, out of a frame that was measured at 0.35 s. initial_population = -1 fills to capacity during _ready, freeze_arrivals holds every body (including the hidden template) where the law put it, spawn_seed pins the draws so one value is one arrangement rather than a fresh object per boot. WHAT THE FIXTURE HIDES, stated rather than buried: frozen, `spigot` photographs as ONE cube, because that is literally what the placement law does. In a lived map the coincident arrivals are shoved apart by collision into a heap, so the tile shows the rule and not the pile it settles into. All three flags ship OFF and no placement sees them.
dna.default: dispersal=spigot, capacity=20 - spigot returns spawn_position and takes NO draw at all, so the global RNG stream is consumed exactly as before (the only other draw, next_spawn_time, moved from randf() to _rf(0.0, 1.0), which with spawn_seed=0 is randf_range(0.0, 1.0) = one identical draw off the same stream); capacity=20 is `const MAX_CUBES: int = 20`, kept in the file and used as the export's default so the default is provably the constant it replaced. play_wood_sound is now passed the cube's own position, which under spigot IS spawn_position. apply_grid_config was `pass` and now returns having touched nothing unless a key is present; it never tears down, and a dispersal change is deliberately not retroactive. The 4 placements spawn the same column they always spawned.
dna.was: three exports (cube_size, gutter, spawn_position - two of them dead: total_size is computed and never used), a `const MAX_CUBES` the file's own @identity block named as the critical parameter, and an apply_grid_config whose entire body was `pass`, so nothing was reachable from a map token. The registry described it as an algorithm that 'randomly generates and places objects in the environment' and the placement was the one thing never left to chance: every cube in the artifact's life entered at exactly spawn_position. The randomness was all in the clock and the kill.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-05, refused by the runner as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. dispersal's values are ecology's three textbook dispersion patterns (random / clumped / even) plus `spigot`, which names the shipped degenerate case - a point process with zero variance - honestly. Ecology is this file's own vocabulary already: carrying capacity, metabolism, 'each spawn requires a death'. THE WORD WAS NOT BORROWED FROM random_cubes: its `macrostate` (uniform|corner|layered|spilled) asks which REGION a fixed pile occupies so the ways-it-could-have-been can be counted, and none of its four values can name a single point. Same substrate, different question, so taking the word would have meant taking it without its answers. DECLINED here: the mortality rule (uniform vs oldest-first vs newest-first is a real argument about memorylessness, but a wooden cube carries no visible age, so four rules photograph as one heap), the 0.3-1.3 s interval, and the wood-knock synthesis - a rate and a sound, both invisible to a still.

rectcube.description: Flat rectangular cube platform (1.0 x 0.2 x 1.0)
rectcube.name: Rectangular Cube
rectcube.qfep_connection: Squash a cube to 0.2 in Y and it stops being a thing and becomes a place to stand — the same eight vertices and twelve triangles, reclassified as ground by nothing but proportion.

right_triangle_lines.name: right_triangle_lines
right_triangle_lines.qfep_connection: Two cyan legs at a metre each, and the hypotenuse arrives pink and two millimetres thicker — the derived quantity dressed to be noticed. Root two is the first length the metre grid cannot say, and the colour scheme admits it.

righttriangle.capacity: READ which properties survive rotation and translation because the right angle stays invariant.

dna.default: proportion=isoceles + reading=uniform - both legs were hard-coded to triangle_size and the slab was a single uniform black surface, so the default rebuilds the original mesh vertex-for-vertex and adds no extra nodes; all 16 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: No exports at all. base_color and triangle_size were plain private vars, the two legs were both pinned to triangle_size (the isoceles case), and there was no apply_grid_config(). The artifact's stated truth - that the right angle is the invariant surviving motion - was never spoken by the form itself, which read as one mute black wedge. proportion turns the claim over: isoceles argues that the metre grid cannot name the hypotenuse, 3-4-5 argues that the rope-stretchers could build it with knots, 1-2 generates root five, kepler puts the sides in golden ratio. reading decides whether the form names its invariant out loud: corner_marked adds the draughtsman's square glyph at the origin, legs_hypotenuse colours the two given sides against the derived third.
dna.note: Existing set_base_color() and set_triangle_size() were also broken before this pass - both reached for get_child(0), which is the scene's embedded Camera3D, not the mesh. The parts list added here fixes that.

righttriangle.description: A right triangle presented as a clean spatial reference. Translation and rotation can move it anywhere, but the ninety-degree relation remains the defining invariant. That makes it useful for reading orientation, perpendicularity, and angular preservation against more complex scenes. It keeps the idea of the right angle available as a diagnostic form.
interactions: place the triangle beside rotating geometry as a reference
compare its hypotenuse and legs under different orientations
use it to read perpendicular relationships in the room
inspect how a thin 2D form behaves inside 3D space
righttriangle.name: righttriangle
righttriangle.qfep_connection: Transformation changes position and orientation while the right angle stays invariant. The artifact isolates what geometric identity survives motion.

rock_primitive.name: Rock
rock_primitive.qfep_connection: Eight authored vertices impersonating geology: the 'rock' is a pyramid with its apex dragged to the origin, and the box collider quietly disagrees with the mesh by twenty percent. Irregularity here is composed, not accumulated.

rock_scanner.description: Dimensional scanner - reveals 2D cross-sections of 3D irregular forms, showing how dimensionality affects perception
rock_scanner.name: Rock Scanner
rock_scanner.qfep_connection: The plane sweeps and the display renders each rock's slice as a filled circle computed from its bounding sphere — a comment in the code admits the substitution as 'simpler and more reliable.' An instrument of dimensional honesty with an idealizing core: the cross-section of the irregular drawn as the one shape no rock has.

rock_spawner.description: Spawns multiple irregular rocks with physics - demonstrates packing inefficiency and gaps
rock_spawner.name: Rock Spawner
rock_spawner.qfep_connection: Thirty seeded irregulars dropped from three and a half metres and left to the solver: the gaps in the settled pile are the lesson. Spheres would pack and boxes would stack — these can't, and the leftover voids are what individuality costs in storage, entropy made legible as trapped air.

rockfactory.description: Generates collections of irregular procedural rocks to demonstrate gaps and packing. Supports multiple spawn modes (box, pile, grid, ring, cluster) and optional gravity.
rockfactory.name: Rock Factory
rockfactory.qfep_connection: Twenty deformed spheres, and the lesson lives in what they fail to fill — gaps are what irregular bodies produce when asked to share space. The pride-colors toggle turns a packing demo into a claim about who arranged the pile.

rockfactory_gravity.description: Rock factory pre-configured with gravity enabled - spawns rocks that fall and settle into containers, demonstrating natural packing and gaps between irregular forms.
rockfactory_gravity.name: Rock Factory (Gravity)
rockfactory_gravity.qfep_connection: Same factory, one boolean flipped: the arrangement is no longer authored but settled, each rock's rest pose an unrepeatable negotiation with its neighbours. The physics solver, not the artist, signs the pile.

rotating_cube.description: A mysterious rotating cube that triggers the first learning sequence
rotating_cube.name: Rotating Cube
rotating_cube.qfep_connection: oscillation: a cube in steady rotation — the room's metronome; period made visible.

rotation_match_puzzle.description: Vera MolnÃ¡r-inspired rotation puzzle. Match cube rotations to ghost targets. Config: style:molnar|interruptions|random|gradient, grid_x:3, grid_z:3, max_rot:45, tolerance:10, axis:z
rotation_match_puzzle.name: Rotation Match Puzzle
rotation_match_puzzle.qfep_connection: Molnár's (Dés)Ordres run in reverse: the canvas shows its disorder as ghost outlines and asks the hand to reproduce it within ten degrees. Restoring noise turns out to be harder than restoring order — E_flux has an exact shape.

dna.default: roughness=0.05, rock_seed=0 - the two hard-coded constants read straight out of the shipped build (the +/-0.05 jitter and the unshifted per-vertex hash), so all 10 existing placements generate the identical mesh
dna.was: zero exports, though its own @identity named noise_seed as the critical parameter and asked for a slider: a fixed eight-point hull perturbed by a hash nobody could reach
dna.argues: roughness=0.0 switches the noise term off and shows the regular polyhedron underneath - the thing the irregularity was irregular ON. Past ~0.2 the fixed face list can no longer close a convex hull and the rock breaks into shards: the boundary where controlled randomness stops being controlled.

roughrock.description: Irregular rock polyhedron created from noise-perturbed vertices.
roughrock.name: roughrock
roughrock.qfep_connection: A rock made by roughing up a polyhedron — vertices pushed out by noise until the clean solid becomes stone. The primitive meeting the randomness chapter early: proof that the organic is just the geometric with its corners disturbed, and that nature's shapes are ideal ones under perturbation.

scale_lines.description: [100m, 10m, 1m, 10cm, 1mm] — a logarithmic ladder of reference lengths made tangible
scale_lines.name: scale_lines
scale_lines.qfep_connection: A logarithmic ladder made tangible — 100m, 10m, 1m, 10cm, 1mm — the reference lengths that give every other measurement meaning. The primitive of scale itself: before a size can be read, a ruler of sizes must exist, and this exhibit is the chapter admitting that even measurement needs its own furniture.

dna.default: rungs=world, arrangement=ladder - the shipped magnitudes at the shipped stacking heights, centred on the axis, so the 8 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: a single literal array holding both the magnitudes and their heights: the ladder could only be 100m/10m/1m/10cm/1mm stacked at fixed y, and the decade it skips (10cm straight to 1mm) could not be read as a choice because no unbroken ladder existed to compare it with

scifi_panel_wall.description: A futuristic panel wall with procedural greebles and atmospheric lighting
scifi_panel_wall.name: Sci-Fi Panel Wall
scifi_panel_wall.qfep_connection: One box mesh; the architecture is entirely in the shader, and every instance duplicates its material and rolls a fresh seed so no two walls repeat. Difference costs a single float — the cheapest possible escape from the tyranny of the tile.

simple_rock.description: Simple irregular rock made from wiggled low-poly sphere - falls with physics
simple_rock.name: Simple Dynamic Rock
simple_rock.qfep_connection: Each vertex is nudged by a hash of its own coordinates, so the deformation is chaos you could regrow identically; the only genuine accident left is the tumble when the rigid body wakes. Reproducible irregularity, with contingency outsourced to gravity.

sliding_door.description: Door that slides left/right on X axis. Teaches translation along a single axis with visual rail and position marker.
sliding_door.name: Sliding Door

small_subdivision_cube.name: small_subdivision_cube
small_subdivision_cube.qfep_connection: Subdivision at hand scale: a cube split into its own smaller selves, the volume version of the Koch move — one artifact you can circle that holds the whole idea of scale recursion.

snap_demo.name: snap_demo
snap_demo.qfep_connection: Six loose grabbable points and a ladder printed on the label: two make a line, three a triangle, four a tetrahedron. Dimension is not a container you enter but a count of commitments between neighbours.

Geometry earning habitability, six vertices at a time.

snap_pyramid_puzzle.name: Snap Pyramid Puzzle
snap_pyramid_puzzle.qfep_connection: Connect five snap points and a square pyramid assembles itself — then becomes a walkable space. The chapter's deepest trick in one gesture: build the primitive correctly and it stops being an object and becomes a *place* you can enter. Geometry earning habitability.

snap_tetrahedron_puzzle.description: Interactive puzzle where connecting 4 snap points forms a tetrahedron that spawns a cube.
snap_tetrahedron_puzzle.name: Snap Tetrahedron Puzzle

snap_wedge_puzzle.description: Interactive puzzle where connecting 6 snap points forms a wedge/prism that spawns a walkable ramp.
snap_wedge_puzzle.name: Snap Wedge Puzzle
snap_wedge_puzzle.qfep_connection: Six connections buy a prism, and the prize is infrastructural — the completed wedge stands in for a ramp you can walk up. Geometry graduates from being looked at to being load-bearing.
