sphere.description: Standard grid-shaded sphere primitive for basic geometry demonstrations.
sphere.name: sphere
sphere.qfep_connection: The sphere, plainly — the primitive of perfect roundness, every point equidistant from a center. The shape antiquity thought the heavens were made of, standing here grid-shaded and ordinary, the baseline against which the low/mid/high tessellations measure how much smoothness costs.

dna.default: tessellation=high (rings=16, radial_segments=16), facets=shown - these are the literals the script has always used and the SimpleGrid material it has always worn, so all 11 existing placements are byte-identical
dna.was: rings and radial_segments are this artifact's own declared critical_parameter and were two literals hard-coded in _ready(), with no apply_grid_config() at all. The trio sphere_low/mid/high spent three tokens making one argument that no single token could state. The grid material was likewise fixed, so the mesh could only ever confess its triangles, never stage the smoothness illusion it exists to deny.
dna.note: tessellation is not a size knob - the object's proportions are unchanged at every value. What changes is whether it admits to being a polyhedron. facets is the paired claim: same geometry, shaded as a surface (hidden) it reads smooth, which is the lie the truth line is arguing against. The axis is named facets rather than skin because MeshInstance3D already owns a skin property and the export would not have compiled.
dna.doc_discrepancy: The description string and the file header both said 32 rings / 32 segments; the shipping code has always been 16. The default is pinned to the code (high=16), not the claim; 32 is now reachable as tessellation=ultra.

sphere_high.description: High poly sphere with 32 rings and 32 radial segments for smooth appearance.
sphere_high.name: sphere_high
sphere_high.qfep_connection: The sphere at 32 rings and segments — smooth to the eye, the illusion complete. Set beside its low-poly siblings it makes the chapter's quiet point about representation: the curve was never real, only approached, and 'smooth' is just 'faceted' with the facets small enough to forgive.

sphere_low.description: Low poly sphere with 8 rings and 8 radial segments showing tessellation structure.
sphere_low.name: sphere_low
sphere_low.qfep_connection: The sphere at 8 rings — faceted, blunt, honest about its lie. The low-poly exhibit that shows what a sphere really is underneath: not a curve but a *decision* about how many flat triangles will stand in for one, curvature confessed as an illusion held by enough small planes.

dna.default: grain=meridian, facets=shown - rings=1, radial_segments=10 exactly as shipped, so all 10 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: rings=1 and radial_segments=10 read as 'low resolution' but are a low resolution spent ENTIRELY IN ONE DIRECTION - ten meridians, no parallels, a lantern rather than a ball. All three grain values spend the same ~20 quads and disagree about where they go, so the knob changes WHICH failure of the approximation you are looking at
dna.note: declaration completed by hand - the promoting agent wrote the script and died on the session limit before declaring the axes

dna.default: resolution=mid (rings=7, radial_segments=7), budget_bias=even - these are the two literals the script has always used and the isotropic split it has always assumed, so all 10 existing placements are byte-identical
dna.was: rings and radial_segments are this artifact's own declared critical_parameter and were two hard-coded 7s in _ready(), with no apply_grid_config() at all. Because they were always equal, the trio sphere_low/mid/high could argue about HOW MUCH resolution a sphere is given but never about WHERE it is spent.
dna.note: budget_bias is the axis that belongs to the middle term specifically, and it is not a size knob - the sphere keeps radius 0.5 and height 1.0 at every value. n*2 rings by n/2 segments (latitude) and its transpose (longitude) hold the face count in the same neighbourhood as n by n, so what you see is the same budget spent in a direction: a barrel of stacked bands, or an orange cut into gores. The truth line says resolution is a budget decision; a budget is spent somewhere, not merely sized. resolution is the amount axis, kept name-compatible in spirit with sphere_high's tessellation.
dna.doc_discrepancy: The description string says 16 rings / 16 radial segments; the shipping code and the artifact's own @identity block both say 7. The default is pinned to the code (mid=7), not the description; 16 is now reachable as resolution=fine.

sphere_mid.description: Medium poly sphere with 16 rings and 16 radial segments for balanced detail.
sphere_mid.name: sphere_mid
sphere_mid.qfep_connection: The sphere at 16 segments — the balanced compromise, smooth enough to read as round, coarse enough to still see the seams. The middle term of the tessellation lesson: every smooth surface in this world is a budget, and this is what a reasonable budget buys.

square_pyramid.description: Johnson Solid J1: Square pyramid with 4 triangular faces and 1 square base.
square_pyramid.name: square_pyramid
square_pyramid.qfep_connection: J1, the smallest name in Norman Johnson's census of ninety-two: four triangles pitched over a square, delegated entirely to a shared factory. The catalogue is the real artifact; this scene just cites entry one.

dna.default: points=5, waist_radius=0.25 - these are the constants the shipped 22-vertex table encodes, and at the default the code returns that literal table verbatim rather than regenerating it, so all 10 existing placements get byte-identical geometry with no float drift
dna.was: zero exports: a five-pointed star hard-coded as 22 literal vertices and 40 literal face indices, a magic table with no way in
dna.argues: reading the table back shows it is not a magic list at all - ten rim points at 36-degree steps alternating radius 0.25 and 0.50. Turning points and waist_radius asks where a star stops: at 12 points it is a sun or a gear, at waist 0.45 the arms sink into a polygon, at 0.10 they become needles. The artifact's own truth is 'form is data'; the axes show that the data itself has an author.

star_primitive.name: Star
star_primitive.qfep_connection: A five-pointed star given thickness — the primitive of the emblem, the shape that means before it measures. The one exhibit here whose geometry is mostly semantic: five points, a pentagram's ghost, proof that even the alphabet of pure form carries meanings it did not ask for.

static_point.description: Non-pickable point marker that displays position. Cannot be grabbed by hands or captured by gravity gun.
static_point.name: Static Point

steppedpyramid.name: Stepped Pyramid
steppedpyramid.qfep_connection: The exports promise a parametric ziggurat — sides, steps, reduction — but the vertices are a frozen Blender export, and number_of_steps only rescales the fossil. A procedural interface stretched over baked geometry: the knobs deform history instead of regrowing it.

tetrahedron.description: Procedural tetrahedron mesh rendered with the project grid material.
tetrahedron.name: tetrahedron
tetrahedron.qfep_connection: Four vertices at alternating corners of a cube, chosen so no two share an edge: the simplex extracted from the box by disagreement. The minimal solid arrives not by building up but as what remains when a cube keeps only every other promise.

tetrahedron_edit.description: Tetrahedron with draggable vertex handles. 4 vertices, 4 faces.
tetrahedron_edit.name: Editable Tetrahedron
tetrahedron_edit.qfep_connection: Four grabbable vertices and a mesh that rebuilds every frame the hand disagrees with it: the simplex held open as a live negotiation. Drag the apex through its own base and nothing objects — the handles keep no orthodoxy about what a tetrahedron must remain.

torus.description: Grid material torus primitive for layout and shading tests.
torus.name: torus
torus.qfep_connection: Two circles multiplied — a path of eight rings, a tube of four segments — and each circle gets its own resolution knob in the map token. The hole is the invariant: coarsen either number and the genus stays one; no sampling decision can close it.

torus_low.description: Low poly torus with 8 ring segments and 6 radial segments showing donut structure.
torus_low.name: torus_low
torus_low.qfep_connection: Six rings by eight segments with the wireframe brightness pushed to 3.5 — the scaffolding lit harder than the surface it holds. A donut that leads with its own triangulation: the seams are the exhibit, smoothness merely their rumor.

dna.default: hole=ring, ring_segments=8 - ring writes inner_radius 0.3 and outer_radius 0.5, the exact pair torus_radials_rings.tscn already carries, and ring_segments is not touched by this promotion at all. All 11 placements render byte-identical; the nine that pass #config:8:4 still set their own segment count, and apply_grid_config now rebuilds only when a value actually changed instead of on every deferred call
dna.was: two exports, and both of them resolution: rings and ring_segments cut the SAME fixed donut into more or fewer triangles. inner_radius 0.3 and outer_radius 0.5 sat as hard-coded numbers nobody ever varied, and their ratio is not a size setting - it is which torus this is. The file's truth statement claims genus 1, one hole, and the artifact had no way to show the hole closing

axis_notes.hole: the ratio of tube radius to path radius, which Godot's TorusMesh derives from the inner/outer pair. hoop 0.45/0.5 is a wire; ring 0.3/0.5 is the shipped donut; thick 0.12/0.5 nearly shuts it; horn 0.001/0.5 makes tube = path and the hole closes to a single point. horn is the value that earns the axis - the genus claim printed in this file's own @identity meets the case where it stops holding. outer_radius is pinned at 0.5 for every value so the silhouette does not grow and the axis cannot be mistaken for scale
axis_notes.ring_segments: the artifact's declared critical_parameter, exported since it shipped but never declared here, so the sweep could not reach it. Sample points along the tube cross-section: at 3 the tube is a triangular prism, at 32 it is round. A previously measured pairwise sweep of 2 vs 4 already moved 3.8% of frame

torus_radials_rings.description: Configurable torus with rings and ring segments. Usage: torus_radials_rings:90:1:#inner:0.2#outer:0.6 or #config:16:8 for 16 rings and 8 ring segments.
torus_radials_rings.name: Torus Radials Rings
torus_radials_rings.qfep_connection: The torus with its resolution exposed — rings around the tube, segments around the ring, both adjustable. The donut as a lesson in double curvature: the only primitive here you cannot flatten without tearing, and the dials show it being built the only way it can be, one quad ring stacked around another.

trafficcone.description: Orange traffic cone with white stripes and square base. Construction site safety marker.
trafficcone.name: Traffic Cone
trafficcone.qfep_connection: White bands laid at 0.30 and 0.55 of the height, twelve radial segments: the whole vocabulary of hazard rebuilt as geometry. The cone itself is innocent — the stripes carry the institution.

transform_staircase_dna.description: DNA double helix: two interleaved spirals. Array + rotation + phase offset.
transform_staircase_dna.name: transform_staircase_dna
transform_staircase_dna.qfep_connection: The double helix is a spiral staircase plus its phase-shifted twin: same array, same rotation-per-step, offset half a turn. Heredity's most sacred icon reduces to one loop read twice at different phases.

transform_staircase_fibonacci.description: Fibonacci spiral: array + golden angle (137.5Â°) + scaling. Nature's growth pattern.
transform_staircase_fibonacci.name: transform_staircase_fibonacci
transform_staircase_fibonacci.qfep_connection: One box repeated, each copy turned 137.5 degrees and scaled by a constant ratio: growth as compound interest on a single seed transform. The golden angle is not decoration — it is why no step ever falls in another's shadow.

transform_staircase_mobius.description: MÃ¶bius strip: array + rotation + twist. One-sided surface, topological oddity.
transform_staircase_mobius.name: transform_staircase_mobius
transform_staircase_mobius.qfep_connection: Treads arrayed around a ring while each absorbs its share of one half-twist: locally every step is an honest stair, globally the surface has quietly given up having two sides. Orientation is a promise kept only in the small.

transform_staircase_showcase.description: All five staircase types together: Linear, Spiral, DNA, Fibonacci, MÃ¶bius. Culmination of arrays + transformation.
transform_staircase_showcase.name: transform_staircase_showcase
transform_staircase_showcase.qfep_connection: Five silhouettes, one script: linear, spiral, DNA, Fibonacci and Möbius are the same loop over step_count with a different transform composed per index, distinguished by nothing but an enum value. Family resemblance made literal — variation as a switch statement over repetition.

transform_staircase_spiral.description: Spiral staircase: array + rotation + translation. Rainbow helix ascending through space.
transform_staircase_spiral.name: transform_staircase_spiral
transform_staircase_spiral.qfep_connection: Fifteen degrees and twelve centimetres per step, compounded — a helix is just a loop that refuses to close. The rainbow gradient indexes every copy, so repetition stays countable even as it becomes architecture.

transformation_cube.description: A mysterious rotating cube that triggers the first learning sequence
transformation_cube.name: transformation_cube
transformation_cube.qfep_connection: a cube cycling its transforms — the transformation family's ambassador in the wave rooms.

translation_demo.description: Two blocking obstacles demonstrating X and Y axis translation. Red obstacle slides horizontally, blue obstacle slides vertically. Obstacles turn green when path is cleared.
translation_demo.name: Translation Demo
translation_demo.qfep_connection: Two axes taught as grievances: a red bar that yields only sideways, a blue one that yields only upward, each turning green once shoved 0.8 past its post. Translation is learned not as a vector but as the direction in which a refusal finally gives.

triangle.description: Interactive triangle mesh with draggable vertices and presets for equilateral, right-angled, and isosceles shapes.
triangle.name: triangle
triangle.qfep_connection: Three points, and suddenly there is an *inside*: the first shape that encloses, the minimum fence. Drag its vertices through equilateral, right, and scalene and feel identity survive deformation — the triangle is where position becomes area, and the plane gets its atom.

dna.default: sidedness=two_tone + convention=none is a no-op. _build_triangle still emits the front face v0,v1,v2 with triangle_color_front and normal +Z and then the back face v1,v0,v2 with triangle_color_back and normal -Z, in that order, through a _face() helper that makes exactly the set_color / set_normal / three add_vertex calls the inline code made; material, tilt, stick, node names and build order are untouched, and convention=none adds no child at all. All 8 placements (8 map_data.json files by direct count, none of which passes a config key) are unchanged. apply_grid_config keeps its old contract too: height, size, tilt and color still set the field and still rebuild nothing, exactly as before, so the only thing that can now tear a placed parasol down is a DNA axis whose value actually differs from the one already built.
dna.was: seven exported floats and colours, and no way to change what the object argues. The double-sided scheme - the artifact's entire subject - was hard-coded as two literal add_vertex runs, and apply_grid_config set four fields that no code ever re-read afterwards, so all eight placements were identical and could not have been otherwise.
dna.note: A triangle is three points IN AN ORDER, and that order is the only thing that gives a flat sheet a front and a back. This parasol exists to make that visible and could previously make the case one way only. sidedness is what the surface claims: two_tone is the shipped flag, flat withdraws the claim entirely (one neutral colour on both faces - what a triangle looks like when nobody has decided which way it faces, and the honest opposite of the artifact's own thesis), inverted keeps the geometry and reverses the naming, which is the point that front and back are a convention rather than a property, and split brings the two colours onto ONE face along the median so facing stops being a secret you have to walk around to learn. convention is the notation the claim is written in: graphics states orientation twice, as a surface normal and as a winding order, they encode the same fact, neither is visible, and the shipped parasol drew neither and asked you to take the colour on faith. normal stands the vector off the face; winding puts arrowheads on the rim in v0 -> v1 -> v2, which is the traversal that decided which face was the front in the first place; both lets the two languages be compared.
dna.kin: `facets` (grab_trihedron, sphere_high, sphere_low: shown|hidden|only) was considered and declined - it asks whether a tessellation is legible, not which side of a surface you are on. `handedness` (VectorCrossProduct: right|left|both) is closer in subject and still wrong: it names the chirality of a coordinate frame, and this sheet has no frame, only two faces. So both words are the artifact's own. `attach` (point: float|stake|plate) and `mode` (request_note: float|plate|stake|decal) govern how an object meets the world it sits in; the parasol's mounting is not in question here and neither list transfers.
dna.harness_note: All four sidedness values differ head-on by design - full pink, full neutral, full blue, and a half-and-half face - so a front-ish camera separates them; a rear-only angle would collapse two_tone and inverted into each other and read as a dead axis when the axis is the thing being photographed. convention=normal and convention=both stand an arrow about 0.32 x triangle_size off the plane, which grows the AABB along +Z and will pull a fit-by-diagonal camera back on those two tiles; the sheet is 0.51 x 0.51 x 0.01 measured, so consider dna.framing if the tiles disagree on scale.

parasol_triangle.description: A triangle mounted on a thin stick like a parasol. Double-sided (pink front, blue back) to show orientation. Place multiples for a forest of triangle flags.
parasol_triangle.name: Parasol Triangle
parasol_triangle.qfep_connection: A triangle on a stick, pink front and blue back, held up like a parasol so you can catch it lying. The double-sided honesty of a face: which way it points is not decoration but data, the primitive teaching that a surface has an opinion about front and back.

triangle_line_puzzle.description: Interactive puzzle: drag 3 line endpoints to form an equilateral triangle.
triangle_line_puzzle.name: Triangle Line Puzzle

dna.default: target_plane=upright, stock=racked - upright maps the canonical triangle back to the shipped literals (0,-0.173,-0.2), (0,-0.173,0.2), (0,0.173,0) and racked returns the three parallel lines at x=0.2, y=-0.2/-0.3/-0.4 verbatim, so all 7 existing placements start in exactly the layout they had before
dna.was: Both tables were hard-coded literals in _init(): one equilateral triangle standing in the local ZY plane, and three identical parallel lines racked beside it. The artifact's own truth line says three points define a unique PLANE, but the plane was never a choice - every placement argued it from the same picture-on-a-wall angle, and the parts were always issued from the same rack. The subclass exported nothing and had no apply_grid_config().
dna.note: target_plane is the argument axis: ground lays the same three points flat so you assemble a floor facet (the triangle as the atomic unit of mesh geometry) instead of a sign, and tilted removes both readings so the plane has to be chosen rather than assumed. stock changes what the act of solving is - racked is assembly from interchangeable parts, strewn is recognition imposed on debris, ringed parks each line just outside the edge it belongs to so the whole puzzle collapses to closure. ringed follows target_plane, so the two axes compose.

triangle_line_puzzle.qfep_connection: Drag three endpoints until the sides are equal — an equilateral triangle, discovered rather than drawn. The puzzle where the hand meets the plane's first enclosure and learns that 'equilateral' is a *condition* satisfied, three lengths agreeing, the simplest fairness a shape can hold.

triangleprofiles.description: Folded pink zigzag profile built from alternating peaks with drag points to edit the pleated surface.
triangleprofiles.name: 1.2: A triangleprofilese
triangleprofiles.qfep_connection: A pleated pink zigzag — alternating peaks folded into a profile you can edit by dragging. The primitive of the fold shown as a section: how a flat strip, creased in a rhythm, becomes a surface with strength and shadow. The chapter's handshake with form-finding and origami, one ribbon deep.

triangular_cupola.description: Johnson Solid J3: Triangular cupola combining triangular and square faces.
triangular_cupola.name: triangular_cupola
triangular_cupola.qfep_connection: J3 is a treaty between polygons that refuse to tile together: a triangle roofs a hexagon through an alternating belt of squares and triangles, and the seam holds. The factory call underneath admits these solids are citations from a finished census, not inventions.

triangularblock.description: Triangular block mesh with matched convex collision for kitbashing.
triangularblock.name: triangularblock
triangularblock.qfep_connection: Mesh and convex collider built from the same four points — what the eye sees is exactly what the solver touches, a rare honesty in a registry full of approximated hulls. A wedge whose entire vocation is adjacency: kitbash currency, worth nothing except against other blocks.

trihedron.name: trihedron
trihedron.qfep_connection: Three triangles share an apex and the base face is simply never written — the solid is open underneath, legible as a body only from the angles it was built to be seen from. Closure turns out to be optional when the viewpoint is policed.

truncatedtetrahedron.description: tetrahedron with corners cut — each vertex replaced by a triangular face, adding 4 new faces. DNA: truncation is how deep the cut goes as a fraction of the body (the parameter the Archimedean family is indexed by); origin_solid decides whether the un-cut tetrahedron stands around the result as a translucent shell, so the cut reads as a subtraction. Config: #truncation:0.9#origin_solid:ghost

dna.default: truncation=0.5, origin_solid=hidden - 0.5 reproduces the previous mesh vertex for vertex (corner vertices at ±0.1 against a body of ±0.2) and hidden is the result shown alone, so the 11 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: zero exports. The artifact claims truncation is an OPERATION and then showed exactly one frozen output of it: the cut depth lived as the bare literal 0.1 in a vertex array, a ratio of one half against the body's 0.2, named nowhere. An operation you can only ever see one result of is indistinguishable from a shape.
dna.note: origin_solid=ghost answers the question the static version could not — cut from WHAT. It closes the seed tetrahedron's four faces on the same corner vertices and stands them around the result unshaded at 16% alpha.

truncatedtetrahedron.name: truncatedtetrahedron
truncatedtetrahedron.qfep_connection: A tetrahedron with its corners cut — each vertex replaced by a triangular face, the simplest Archimedean solid. The primitive that shows how truncation makes a new regular form from an old one: slice the points off the minimal solid and thirteen semi-regular cousins become possible. Geometry reproducing by amputation, the Platonic set giving birth to the Archimedean.

unitcube.description: Unit cube from vertex and face arrays
unitcube.name: Unit Cube
unitcube.qfep_connection: Eight vertices and twelve winding-ordered triangles written out longhand: the cube taken back from the engine's built-in primitive and re-earned as data. The 0.5 scale factor confesses its origin — born two-by-two-by-two, disciplined down to the grid's unit.

wood_cube.name: wood_cube
wood_cube.qfep_connection: Grain without growth: a shader computes rings from position — ring_scale, wave_scale, a little noise — on a ten-centimetre pickable box. The tree is gone; what the hand closes around is a texture law wearing timber's uniform.

zigzagprofile.description: Interactive zigzag strip featuring top and base grab points plus presets for zigzag, sine, and sawtooth patterns.
zigzagprofile.name: 1.2: A zigzagprofile
zigzagprofile.qfep_connection: Five folds held between two rows of grab spheres — peaks at 70%, valleys at 30% — and every point freezes where you drop it. The pleat becomes a negotiation record: each rigid vertex is a decision made and not yet reopened.

achilles_tortoise.description: Zeno's paradox of Achilles and the Tortoise. Watch infinite steps converge to a finite limit: A_n = L*(1-1/2^n). Each step halves the gap — infinite steps, finite distance. The paradox dissolves in the limit.
achilles_tortoise.name: Achilles and the Tortoise
achilles_tortoise.qfep_connection: Zeno's race staged as steps that shrink toward a limit — Achilles gaining forever and arriving anyway. The paradox that made mathematicians distrust infinity for two thousand years, standing in the primitives room as a warning: the simplest setup, a runner and a lead, contains a crack that took calculus to seal.

mesh_builder_demo.name: Mesh Builder Demo
mesh_builder_demo.description: Interactive mesh construction from primitives. Add vertices as spheres, connect them with edges, fill triangles as colored faces. Shows how meshes are built from points, lines, and faces.

klee_walking_point.description: A luminous point that sets itself in motion and leaves a trail of points - the trail IS a line. Klee's Pedagogical Sketchbook page one: an active line on a walk. walk_style: 'meander' (queer wander) vs 'straight' (collapsed shortest path).

dna.default: walk_style=meander, line=active - the shipped picture exactly. line=active takes the identical code path _walk_path always took and builds no extra geometry, and walk_style=meander is the branch the existing match already fell through to, so all 20 placements are bit-identical. None of the 20 passes a config key.
dna.was: walk_style was already an export and already this file's own declared critical_parameter, but as a free String nothing enumerated: the sweep read the artifact as having no turnable knob, no map ever named a value, and 20 placements all showed the same open ochre meander. The artifact argues a line is a biography and shipped exactly one biography. apply_grid_config also tore down and rebuilt on any call, including a call that changed nothing.
dna.note: walk_style says what the point DID - meander (three summed sines, no goal), straight (the collapsed route that learned nothing on the way), arc (one decision made once), spiral (the walk that keeps turning inside its own territory). line says what the resulting mark IS, taken from the Pedagogical Sketchbook's own opening taxonomy rather than invented: active is the line that goes for a walk, the only kind whose two ends are not the same place; medial is the line circumscribing a figure, the same walk closed on itself so it becomes a boundary instead of a journey - and because the walk's deviation is spent on the radius, a medial meander is not a circle, it is a walk that came back; passive is the line as a plane's edge, where the trail keeps its exact geometry and a surface is raised to the floor beneath it, so the same points read as the top edge of something. All three are one silhouette apart: open string, closed ring, filled field. Everything remains deterministic summed sines - no randf, no noise - which the Primitives sequence requires.
dna.declined: Speed, hold, loop and how-far-the-head-has-got are this artifact's most conspicuous parameters and all four are declined, because the evidence is ONE STILL and a still cannot tell 0.32 from 0.9. Promoting them would have produced a finished-looking experiment answering nothing. 'Is the point that made it still present' was declined for the opposite reason: the head is a 0.04 m sphere and removing it changes too few pixels to read as anything but noise. Both shipped axes are properties of the trail as a standing object, so they survive the shutter.
dna.fixture_why: A capture taken a third of a second after boot catches the walk barely started: the whole trail present but dim, the head at the far left. Running the walk to completion inside the settle and then not looping holds the finished line, fully lit, indefinitely - which is the axis's subject (the trail as a standing object) rather than an accident of shutter timing. loop is parsed from a string inside _read_metadata_overrides, never assigned to the typed bool export directly, which is the trap that eats fixture flags before _ready.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config compares a signature of every value _build reads and returns early when they match, so a no-op reconfigure no longer restarts the walk. Animation values (walk_speed, hold_seconds, loop) are deliberately absent from that signature - _process honours them live and must not throw the geometry away mid-walk.

klee_walking_point.name: Klee Walking Point
klee_walking_point.qfep_connection: A line is a point that refused to stay still. The straight walk learned nothing; the meander is the line at the edge of chaos.

fontana_puncture.description: A solid cube with an oversized sphere subtracted (CSG, baked) so the void breaches every face - Fontana's Concetto Spaziale in 3D. A luminous point floats at the centre.

dna.default: breach=opened, strike=centred - the default pair is a SHORT-CIRCUIT, not a recomputation: _cut_radius() and _cut_offset() return the raw sphere_radius (0.34) and sphere_offset (ZERO) untouched at these values, so all 37 placements are bit-identical, including the 44 exhibit_furniture#mount:fontana_puncture plinth mounts and the 8 that embed interactive_point_origin_force. A placement that names sphere_radius or sphere_offset directly still wins over the named axis - the vocabulary is laid over the raw floats, never in place of them.
dna.was: sphere_radius and sphere_offset are this artifact's own declared critical_parameter and were reachable only as unnamed floats. 37 placements, every one showing the same 0.34 sphere: an artifact whose whole argument is that subtraction is generative, shipping exactly one subtraction.
dna.note: breach is not a size knob - cube_size stays 0.5 at every value, so the object keeps its cell and its footprint. The four values are the four topologically DISTINCT states of this geometry, cut against the cube's own critical distances (half-extent 0.5, edge-midpoint 0.707, corner 0.866 x cube_size): pierced 0.54 = six round mouths in solid matter (Fontana's buchi, dented through but not hollowed); opened 0.68 = shipped, 0.46 m mouths on a 0.5 m face and still connected, a thin frame; severed 0.74 = past the edge-midpoint, the twelve edges cut and the cube surviving as eight disconnected corner pieces, a different OBJECT not a smoother one; husk 0.80 = corners down to a twentieth of the extent. It stops short of 0.866 deliberately - past that the cube is gone and the frame measures NO RENDER, which is a fact about the capture and not about the art. strike is the paired direction axis (the same amount/direction split sphere_mid made with resolution/budget_bias); its three displaced values move on Y or on all three axes at once, so no single camera yaw can hide the axis behind the silhouette. The embedded point and the centre glint both ride the cut, so under strike the point that carved the void is still IN the void rather than buried in the surviving matter.
dna.declined: a third axis for WHAT the cutting tool is - a taglio (slash) against the buchi (holes) - is the obvious next promotion and is the artifact's own art-historical subject. It is not shipped because a slash is a cut in ONE face and the sweep photographs from a single fixed camera: half the yaws would show an uncut cube and the critic would report a fact about camera placement as a verdict on Fontana. Both axes shipped here are spherically or vertically legible, so no frame can lie about them.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config previously tore down and rebuilt on ANY call. It now requires config_data.size() > 0, which preserves every real placement (all pass at least one key, and the 8 embedding ones need the rebuild) while removing the no-op reconfigure churn.

fontana_puncture.name: Fontana Puncture
fontana_puncture.qfep_connection: The point given a radius and aimed at solid matter becomes the absence that defines the form. Subtraction as meaning - the first boolean.

dna.default: deixis=words_and_mark - a no-op. It builds the FloorText node (same TextMesh, same font 96, same pixel_size 0.004, same -PI/2 about X, same y = 0.012) and then the Ring node (same torus, same 48 rings, same y = 0.008), in that order, which is exactly what _build did before the split into _build_words / _build_ring; show_ring is still consulted, so a placement that had turned the ring off still has it off. apply_grid_config now compares the values the build reads before and after applying the config and returns without touching the tree when nothing moved, so curation_station's framing keys no longer tear the decal down and put an identical one back. All 28 placements (29 tokens across 29 maps by direct count) pass no config, so none of them changes by a pixel.
dna.was: the sentence and the mark welded together in one _build. text, text_color, font_size, text_scale, show_ring, ring_radius, ring_color and pride_gradient were all exported, and every one of them changed how the decal LOOKED; none of them changed what it claimed. show_ring came closest and is a bare bool that no registry declared, so the sweep could never reach it.
dna.note: Everything this object is made of is deixis: four words that mean nothing until a body stands over them. The wayfinding decal is a two-part speech act - a claim ('here') and a mark that gives the claim a referent - and the two halves were inseparable. words_only is the claim with nothing marked: still true, and it now says nothing, which is the purest case. mark_only is the corporate blue dot: you are located and nobody addresses you. arrow makes the pointing literal by pointing at the sentence, the only thing a sign like this can indicate. plan_fragment moves the whole scene inside a drawing of the room - walls, a partition, the doorway you came in through - which is the mall-map move, where finding yourself means finding your dot on someone else's plan. That last one is the value the artifact's own truth line was written for: 'the friendliest face of algorithmic capture'.
dna.kin: `presence` was considered and declined. magritte_pipe asks the same question two batches ago - which of the two terms, the sign or the thing, is actually in the frame - but its answers are pipe_and_words|pipe_only|words_only|empty_frame|picture_of_picture and a pipe is not a floor decal, so the list cannot transfer character for character. dark_sphere already holds `presence` with a third list (witness|hush|beacon|eclipse), which is the state a word gets into when it is reused for its shape instead of its answers. So the word here is the artifact's own: deixis, which is what a wayfinding sticker IS. Only the middle values rhyme with magritte's on purpose - words_only means the same thing in both files, a sign with its referent withheld.
dna.harness_note: Flat geometry lying on the floor: fit-by-diagonal will pull the camera far back for plan_fragment (about 4 x 2.9 m of bars) and close in for the others, so read the bite with that in mind and set dna.framing if the tiles disagree on scale. pride_gradient is deliberately NOT an axis - it is a hue cycle in _process, invisible to a still, and the ring and the new plan bars now share one material so it still tints every printed line.

you_are_here.description: A text decal on the floor - YOU ARE HERE lying flat underfoot, the wayfinding locator. A flat indexical inscription you stand ON. TextMesh. pride_gradient reclaims the corporate blue dot.
you_are_here.name: You Are Here
you_are_here.qfep_connection: 'You are here' is what a civilisation writes when it renders every body as a coordinate it has already labelled. The friendliest face of algorithmic capture.

mystic_writing_pad.description: Freud's Mystic Writing-Pad (Wunderblock, 1925) as the trace apparatus: a red-framed magic slate where a stylus writes a bright trace of points on a clearing sheet, and every lift sinks the trace into the wax below as a faint warm ghost. The surface forgets; the depth remembers. Derrida's model of the trace, made a thing you stand before.
mystic_writing_pad.name: Mystic Writing Pad
mystic_writing_pad.qfep_connection: The Mystic Pad lies the way every memory system lies: it shows a clean surface and keeps the wax. 'Clear' is the politest word a machine knows for 'kept, where you can no longer see it' - the trace as the friendly face, and the log, of algorithmic memory.

hand_telemetry_display.description: A big dark Half-Life-2 / Combine-style ops monitor on a grey pipe-clamp arm, streaming the player's RIGHT HAND world position in real time: large orange X/Y/Z numerals plus a scrolling timecoded coordinate log, newest bright and fading down. The point that is watched. Falls back to a demo drift when no XR hand is present.
hand_telemetry_display.name: Hand Telemetry Display
hand_telemetry_display.qfep_connection: The display helps you and records you in the same orange glow: 'you are at (0.42, 1.13, -0.88)' means 'we have you at (0.42, 1.13, -0.88), and at every value before it.' The friendliest face of capture is a monitor that calls surveillance a service.

living_paper.description: A hanging sheet of warm paper that is alive: it breathes (a standing-wave ripple) and reads the player's RIGHT HAND into itself - the paper bulges toward the nearby hand like skin under a touch and blooms a fading ink trace of dots where it passes. The warm counterpart to the telemetry monitor: the trace received, not logged. Phantom-hand fallback for capture.
living_paper.name: Living Paper
living_paper.qfep_connection: The paper that leans toward you and inks your wandering is the tenderest face of the same act the monitor performs coldly: it receives you, keeps a little of you, and it is hard to say where care ends and capture begins - which is exactly the trace.

hand_telemetry_diptych.description: Two Half-Life-2 / Combine-style ops monitors side by side on one grey pipe-clamp mount - a diptych. The LEFT panel (cyan) streams the left hand's live world position, the RIGHT panel (orange) the right hand's, each a scrolling coordinate log. The tracked body split down the middle and read in stereo. Composes two hand_telemetry_display panels.
hand_telemetry_diptych.name: Hand Telemetry Diptych
hand_telemetry_diptych.qfep_connection: You were never watched as a whole, only as a set of hands, each on its own bright channel. The diptych is honest about the plural: a fully captured body is just a list of points, one feed per part.

automatic_writing_desk.description: A desk with a sheet of paper that the headset writes by itself: a pen sweeps left-to-right and drops a row at the margin, filling the page top-to-bottom with asemic script whose jaggedness scales with HEAD speed (still = flat ruled line, moving = jagged handwriting). Surrealist automatic writing / the spiritualist planchette, with the head as the medium. Driven by XRCamera3D; demo head-drift fallback.
automatic_writing_desk.name: Automatic Writing Desk
automatic_writing_desk.qfep_connection: The desk transcribes the one thing you never agreed to author: your attention. A head, sampled as it turns toward whatever it cannot help looking at, is a confession written in a hand you can't read - kept on the page after you walk away.

two_points_line.description: Two luminous endpoints and the segment between them - Euclid's first postulate. Different-coloured points with a messenger travelling A<->B so the line reads as a live channel of relation.
two_points_line.name: Two Points Line
two_points_line.qfep_connection: A line is the first relation in geometry - relation, not substance. Collapse is A=B; the move is difference held apart and bridged without being erased.

horizon_line.description: A horizon - sky over ground meeting at a bright seam that overhangs the frame. Friedrich, Rothko, Munoz's queer horizon: the line as the not-yet, approached and never reached.
horizon_line.name: Horizon Line
horizon_line.qfep_connection: Futurity installed as a primitive: the only line whose definition includes your never reaching it. Munoz's world that is not enough yet.

redline.description: A red line on the floor with two faintly different fields either side - the line that divides. HOLC redlining (1935), the analog ancestor of the classifier's decision boundary. Steppable, which the originals were not.
redline.name: Redline
redline.qfep_connection: The same primitive that connects can sort - sorting, drawn and enforced, is the ancestor of every algorithmic fence. The decision boundary with its map returned.

three_points_triangle.description: Three points, three edges, the moment they close into a surface - the first plane, the GPU's atom. Corner points, edges, a real filled face, the face normal. Everything smooth is secretly faceted.
three_points_triangle.name: Three Points Triangle
three_points_triangle.qfep_connection: Point->line->triangle is the curriculum's first complete sentence: a position, a relation, an enclosed inside. The founding act of all computer graphics.

tensegrity_triangle.description: A triangle of three struts and three joints holding its shape under a load that would fold any other polygon. Fuller: the triangle is the only rigid polygon. A compression pulse it visibly springs back from.
tensegrity_triangle.name: Tensegrity Triangle
tensegrity_triangle.qfep_connection: The triangle as relation made rigid - the first structure that holds itself up. Nature stabilises with triangles because nothing else stays true under load.

pink_triangle.description: A pink triangle on black - the Nazi camp badge turned point-UP by Silence=Death and ACT UP, a banner of refusal. Its orientation is the whole argument. inverted=false is the reclaimed form.
pink_triangle.name: Pink Triangle
pink_triangle.qfep_connection: Queerness coded into the most elementary form - a hinge to the QFEP thesis. Form is never neutral once a body has worn it; the reclaiming 180 degrees is the move made history.

triangle_whiteboard.description: A lab whiteboard with the science of the triangle in marker (TextMesh) - diagram, angle sum, rigidity, the GPU fact. The first scientific-register board (later superseded by the hand-chalk chalkboard).
triangle_whiteboard.name: Triangle Whiteboard
triangle_whiteboard.qfep_connection: The scientific register - the flat truth behind the poetry. A curriculum needs a surface where the answer is written.

chalkboard.description: A framed blackboard with hand-chalked notation in Turing's hand - a ScribbleControl draws real math as wobbly chalk strokes (no font), mapped onto a 3D board. Default: the triangle facts. Content is the lines array.
chalkboard.name: Chalkboard
chalkboard.qfep_connection: A queer-humanist curriculum needs the answer written by a HAND, not typeset by a machine that pretends mathematics fell from the sky. Even 180 degrees was thought by somebody, at a board.

wall_placard.description: A museum wall caption — TITLE, a thin accent rule, sequence-date metadata, and one sentence of intent, in gallery-label typography. The curatorial register of the lab: it CAPTIONS the work (where the chalkboard states the science and the gem enacts it). Replaces the old AnnotationInfoBoard HUD (XP/health/barcode) as the wall caption. Procedural 2D-in-3D, baked to a mipmapped texture so the small body text stays legible at VR distance.
wall_placard.name: Wall Placard

parameters.title: THE POINT
parameters.body: Position without extension. Zero dimensions. The seed of all form.

wall_placard.qfep_connection: Curation is a choice about what is made thinkable; the label decides the one sentence the visitor carries.

point_chalkboard.description: A chalkboard for THE POINT - a chalk dot with crosshair guides: P=(x,y,z), 0 dimensions, the seed of all form.
point_chalkboard.name: Point Chalkboard
point_chalkboard.qfep_connection: Even 'nothing' has a definition - the dimensionless seed every shape grows from.

triangle_chalkboard.description: A mystical chalkboard for THE TRIANGLE - the labelled triangle plus Δ as both shape and symbol: the first plane to close, the only rigid polygon, and change/difference. Ends on a koan, not a formula: 'what is the cost of Δ?'
triangle_chalkboard.name: Triangle Chalkboard
triangle_chalkboard.qfep_connection: Δ is form, change, and difference in one symbol - and to differ, to close a new plane, is never free. The board names the cost without paying it.

line_chalkboard.description: A chalkboard for THE LINE - endpoints A,B and midpoint M: shortest path, length |B-A|, M=(A+B)/2, 1 dimension.
line_chalkboard.name: Line Chalkboard
line_chalkboard.qfep_connection: The line as pure relation - two points imply a unique straight path. The first relation, stated by hand.

quad_chalkboard.description: A chalkboard for THE QUAD - a rectangle with the diagonal: 4 vertices, area w*h, GPU draws 2 triangles, the screen is a quad.
quad_chalkboard.name: Quad Chalkboard
quad_chalkboard.qfep_connection: Every screen is two triangles pretending to be a rectangle. The triangle never left.

qfep_chalkboard.description: A wide chalkboard for the QUEER FREE ENERGY PRINCIPLE - QFE = F - lambda E(S) + phi dE beside an edge-of-chaos curve peaking at lambda~0.4 where life sits between order and noise.
qfep_chalkboard.name: QFEP Chalkboard
qfep_chalkboard.qfep_connection: This IS the QFEP, stated. Life at the edge, not frozen and not noise. The phi-term is the queer one - refusing to settle.

endlessness_chalkboard.description: A chalkboard for ENDLESSNESS - potential vs actual infinity, an inward spiral that never closes. The limit approached but never reached.
endlessness_chalkboard.name: Endlessness Chalkboard
endlessness_chalkboard.qfep_connection: Two infinities: a process with no last step, and the completed whole. Reaching the limit would end the endlessness.

thrownness_chalkboard.description: A chalkboard for THROWNNESS - Heidegger's Geworfenheit: a figure dropped along an arrow into a bounded grid it did not choose. Made literal: spawn is a throw.
thrownness_chalkboard.name: Thrownness Chalkboard
thrownness_chalkboard.qfep_connection: You wake already IN a world, at a place not of your choosing. The grid was here before you. You are here - and here was not your decision.

silhouette_gate.name: Silhouette Gate (draw to open)
silhouette_gate.description: A ghost silhouette of a form. Take the drawing point and trace the form by passing through every vertex; complete it and the form dissolves as a sliding door opens. 2D forms (triangle, square/quad, pentagon, hexagon, circle) AND 3D forms — a cube is a green wireframe whose 8 corners must all be drawn through. Configurable: form, form_size, hit_radius, ordered, ring_points, rotation_offset_deg, door_tag.

archimedean_tunnel.description: The primitives seam. A digital line is a polygon pretending to be a curve — at arm's length the machine's chords read smooth; magnified (the tunnel) they cut every corner, with holes between the samples where the hand was and the machine never looked. Archimedes exhausted the circle with polygons; the machine stops at N.
archimedean_tunnel.name: Archimedean Tunnel
archimedean_tunnel.qfep_connection: A station in the bias landscape (doc/SEAM_PER_SEQUENCE.md); the digital-bias seam for primitives. Bias is conserved; show the seam.

rotating_prisme.name: Rotating Prisme
rotating_prisme.description: A slowly rotating prism — continuous rotation makes orientation legible without interaction. Sibling of prism_block; used in the 2D-colour tutorial as ambient motion reference.
rotating_prisme.qfep_connection: A constant 45 degrees per second is the entire program, and it is enough: a still prism is only a silhouette, so depth here is not shown but accumulated, frame by frame, in the viewer's short-term memory.
